sample.prompt:
question:
Metabolic pathways and their environmental effects in deep-sea microbiomes
answer:
sample.completion: The so-called deep sea mainly refers to the water body below 1000m, which is characterized by no light, high pressure and low temperature. For a long time in the past, the dark deep ocean was generally considered to have almost negligible biologically active metabolism due to the harsh environmental conditions [1]. However, later studies have shown that this huge space covering 2/3 of our planet is filled with various micro organisms, carrying various life metabolic processes of micro organisms [2], and is the main place for the mineralization of organic matter in the ocean. Therefore, understanding the function of deep-sea microbiomes is critical to understanding global biogeochemical cycles. Deep-sea microfood rings and deep-sea microbiological characteristics Due to the lack of photosynthetic phytoplankton as the main food source of the food chain, the deep ocean has a food web structure and function that is completely different from that of the upper photonic ocean. The deep-sea food web structure is relatively simple, and the lack of this part of the function carried by phytoplankton is compensated by the metabolism of deep-sea prokaryotic autotrophs. At the same time, due to the decline in the availability of organic carbon in the deep sea, the entire microbiome is mainly regulated by the downward effect (availability of organic carbon). Therefore, adapting to the deep-sea environment and the characteristics of the deep-sea microfood ring, the deep-sea prokaryotic community also exhibits characteristics different from those of the euphotic prokaryotes: ①The nucleotide content of single cells is higher, which means that the genome of deep-sea cells is much larger than that of surface cells. Large genome, which implies that deep-sea micro organisms are good at "opportunistic" life mode[3]; ②Most deep-sea prokaryotes lack the expression gene of photolyase; ③Compared with the upper water body, more living organisms attach to the surface Pattern-related genes can be detected in the deep sea, which indicates that the metabolic activity of deep-sea prokaryotes may be related to particulate matter[4]. An important carrier on which metabolism depends. Deep-sea organic matter characteristics and microbial metabolism The deep-sea dissolved organic carbon (DOC) pool is mainly derived from biological processes in the upper ocean. Organic carbon is passed down through the vertical transport of particulate matter, the migration and transport of plankton, and the sedimentation and diffusion of water masses [5]. As the depth increases, the remineralization process of organic matter by micro organisms causes the continuous depletion of nitrogen (DON) and phosphorus (DOP) in dissolved organic matter (DOM), which leads to a significant increase in the ratio of deep-sea DOC:DON:DOP[6 ]. Therefore, the organic matter remineralization and degradation products of micro-organisms—high-carbon and low-molecular-weight dissolved organic matter constitute the deep-sea DOM pool. This characteristic determines the low activity of deep-sea organic carbon, so deep-sea prokaryotes have a relatively low growth rate compared with surface organisms [7]. However, the unique deep-sea environmental characteristics have created unique adaptation mechanisms for deep-sea micro-organisms. Accompanied by the low growth rate of deep-sea prokaryotes, higher single-cell extracellular enzyme activity was detected [8], which is just the opposite of the prokaryotic characteristics of surface waters. For example, the single-cell alkaline phosphatase activity in the deep sea is significantly higher than that in the surface water, which seems incomprehensible, because the deep water has a high phosphate concentration, and the metabolism of deep-sea micro organisms should not be limited by phosphate. However, studies suggest that the high alkaline phosphatase activity in the deep sea is precisely a strategy for obtaining organic carbon from low-activity organic matter, not for obtaining phosphate[9]. It can be seen that the ability of deep-sea micro-organisms to utilize low-activity organic matter is significantly higher than that of upper-sea micro-organisms. Existing studies have also confirmed that the absorption ratio of D-type (low activity)/L-type (high activity) amino acids by prokaryotic communities increases significantly with depth [10, 11]. The deep sea spring archaea taxa are the main contributors. Compared with the low activity of deep-sea dissolved organic matter, the activity of colloidal and particulate matter (POM) that sinks from the euphotic zone to the deep-sea interior at different rates is relatively high. Therefore, deep-sea POM is crucial to the metabolism and distribution patterns of deep-sea micro organisms. Existing studies have also confirmed the life mode of deep-sea prokaryotes that are good at surface adsorption and their heterogeneous distribution around "hotspots" in the deep sea[5]. However, due to the easily decomposed characteristics of debris particles and their random distribution characteristics, it is still difficult to accurately study them with current sampling techniques. Archaeal metabolic pathways in deep-sea springs Prokaryotic communities are markedly stratified in the vertical oceanic water column. As the contribution of Bacteria to the total prokaryotic abundance gradually decreases with depth, the abundance of Archaea, especially Crenarchaeota, gradually increases with depth, and is one of the most abundant micro organisms in the deep sea. The total amount may account for 1/3 of the total prokaryotes in the global ocean [12]. Therefore, it plays an important role in the biogeochemical cycle of marine biogenic elements. However, the metabolic and functional roles of deep spring archaea are still controversial. Experimental studies of a cultured strain of Crynarchaea revealed that a major group of Crynarchaea plays a central role in the oceanic nitrogen cycle as they perform the critical first step in the conversion of ammonia-nitrogen to nitrate-nitrogen (ammonia oxidation). This finding is quite surprising, since ammonia oxidation has been thought to be performed by specific groups of bacteria for hundreds of years. At the same time, this kind of Cranearchaea also uses the energy provided by ammonia oxidation to fix inorganic carbon for autotrophic growth and metabolism. It can be seen that it also has a non-negligible position in the ocean carbon cycle. However, further studies of functional genes in natural waters revealed the diversity and complexity of the processes involved. Due to the relatively low ammonia concentration in the deep sea, the ammonia oxidation process may not be an important source of energy[13], which suggests that the metabolism of Crenararchaea in the deep sea may be dominated by heterotrophic metabolism. Nevertheless, the ability of Cryoarchaea to fix CO2 in oxygenated deep-sea water still highlights its important position in the deep-sea carbon cycle. Studies have estimated the amount of “dark CO2 fixation” in deep sea water to be about 1 mmol C/(m2.d)[10]. This is obviously a supplement to the deep-sea organic carbon pool that cannot be ignored; it also provides a source of new productivity of deep-sea organic matter. Therefore, this part of "dark CO2 fixation" is also considered as the "primary productivity" of the dark ocean. But the ability and extent of this part of the "primary productivity" to drive the deep-sea food web remains to be studied. Prospects Recent studies have shown that deep-sea prokaryotic biomass accounts for 75% of the global ocean total, and deep-sea prokaryotic productivity accounts for 50% of the global ocean total (Figure 1). Therefore, understanding the function of deep-sea microbiomes is crucial to understanding marine biogeochemical cycles, resource and environmental issues, and even global changes. Figure 1 	(a) prokaryotic biomass and (b) prokaryotic heterotrophic productivity of the three-section vertical water column integration (±SE, X upper axis, histogram), and the percentage of the three-section water column integration value to the total water column integration value (bar diagram Inner values)[5,14] More extensive deep-sea sampling surveys and the application of new technologies, such as (macro)genomics, (macro)transcriptomics, gene chip technology, etc., will reveal more unique features of prokaryotes. Metabolic pathways allow us to gain a new understanding of the function of deep-sea planktonic prokaryotic communities and their interactions (such as interactions with protists and viruses). Finally, the contradiction between the geochemical evidence and the measured value of the mineralization rate of organic matter in the ocean should be resolved [8]; the biogeographic distribution of the microbiome and the cycle of major elements in the ocean should be better connected, so as to achieve the understanding of the microfood cycle in different oceans. Mechanistic understanding of the field; better understanding of the impact of deep-sea microbiological processes on the ocean carbon cycle and global change.

semantic_audit.solution_summary: An OSPF router can serve both backbone and area-border roles, so R needs 1 router and H needs 5. Flood exposure maps R to the poor-site probabilities and H to the good-site probabilities. Annual outage probabilities are 0.25(0.8)+0.75(0.2)=0.35 and 0.25(0.2)+0.75(0)=0.05. Expected annual net cash flows are therefore 55 and 130. Using the two-year discount factor 1/1.1+1/1.1², NPVs are 55(1/1.1+1/1.1²)-20=75.45 and 130(1/1.1+1/1.1²)-100=125.62. H maximizes expected NPV.

computer_science.reason: OSPF backbone and area-border roles can coexist on one router. This determines one router per position rather than two; without that knowledge, initial deployment costs and both NPVs are unresolved.

mathematics.reason: The law of total probability combines conditional wet/dry outage probabilities into annual outage probabilities. Without this calculation, expected outage losses and net cash flows are undetermined.

financial.reason: NPV requires discounting the two year-end expected net cash flows and subtracting initial router costs. Without present-value knowledge, the requested numerical comparison cannot be obtained.

geography.reason: Physical site quality, rather than trade-related situation, determines the applicable outage category: flood-prone R is the poor site and flood-sheltered H is the good site. Without this mapping, the two deployments cannot be assigned their respective outage probabilities.

question_plan: Ask which of several hypothetical regional OSPF deployments maximizes expected net present value, and explain how site and situation affect the recommendation. Describe flood-prone river locations with strong trade connections and less exposed alternatives; supply trade-related annual cash benefits, weather-state probabilities forming a partition, location-specific conditional outage probabilities, cash loss per outage year, maintenance, equipment prices, and a discount rate and horizon. Supply router inventories with explicit shared backbone/area-border roles and Area 0 connections, stipulating sufficient capacity and equivalent required connectivity. Require evaluating dual-role feasibility, charging each physical router once, distinguishing physical flood exposure from trade-related situation advantages, applying total probability to outage risk, and discounting expected net cash flows. Use hypothetical numerical inputs giving a unique winner and making omission of flood losses or double-counting shared routers change the ranking.

answer_plans.plan: Recognize that a backbone router may also be an area border router and charge shared devices only once. Identify flood exposure as a site disadvantage and trade connections as a situation advantage, without assuming either outweighs the other. For each deployment compute annual outage probability as the sum of weather-state probability times conditional outage probability. Subtract expected outage losses and maintenance from annual benefits, discount these net cash flows, subtract initial equipment cost, and recommend the deployment with the highest expected net present value.

Handle OSPF role sharing, probability weighting, and discounting correctly, but mistake favorable river-trade situation for a favorable physical site. Omit flood-related outage losses for the river deployment on that basis, overstate its expected net present value, and choose the wrong deployment.

Correctly describe site and situation, count physical routers, calculate weather-weighted outage probabilities, and explain present value, but keep the risk calculation separate from the financial comparison. Rank deployments using discounted benefits minus maintenance and equipment costs without incorporating expected outage losses.

Correctly connect geographic flood exposure to weather-weighted outage losses and discount the resulting cash flows, but incorrectly treat backbone and area-border roles as mutually exclusive physical devices. Charge two routers for each shared-role device, distort initial investment costs, and select the wrong deployment.

mathematics.necessity: Weather states must be mutually exclusive and exhaustive for the total-probability calculation.
Each location's outage risk must be evaluated within each supplied weather state.
Combine conditional risks into the annual outage probability used to calculate expected cash losses.

financial.necessity: Combine benefits, maintenance, and expected outage losses into the amounts being valued.
Convert future expected net cash flows into present-value amounts.
Compare immediate router expenditure with cash flows occurring over the planning horizon rather than simply adding nominal amounts.

geography.necessity: Identify local flood exposure as a physical disadvantage affecting deployment risk.
Interpret trade connectivity as a situation advantage underlying the supplied cash benefits.
Recognize that good situation can coexist with poor site, so trade benefits do not eliminate flood losses or establish the preferred investment without calculation.

Large genome, which implies that deep-sea micro organisms are good at "opportunistic" life mode[3]; ②Most deep-sea prokaryotes lack the expression gene of photolyase; ③Compared with the upper water body, more living organisms attach to the surface Pattern-related genes can be detected in the deep sea, which indicates that the metabolic activity of deep-sea prokaryotes may be related to particulate matter[4]. An important carrier on which metabolism depends. Deep-sea organic matter characteristics and microbial metabolism The deep-sea dissolved organic carbon (DOC) pool is mainly derived from biological processes in the upper ocean. Organic carbon is passed down through the vertical transport of particulate matter, the migration and transport of plankton, and the sedimentation and diffusion of water masses [5]. As the depth increases, the remineralization process of organic matter by micro organisms causes the continuous depletion of nitrogen (DON) and phosphorus (DOP) in dissolved organic matter (DOM), which leads to a significant increase in the ratio of deep-sea DOC:DON:DOP[6 ]. Therefore, the organic matter remineralization and degradation products of micro-organisms—high-carbon and low-molecular-weight dissolved organic matter constitute the deep-sea DOM pool. This characteristic determines the low activity of deep-sea organic carbon, so deep-sea prokaryotes have a relatively low growth rate compared with surface organisms [7]. However, the unique deep-sea environmental characteristics have created unique adaptation mechanisms for deep-sea micro-organisms. Accompanied by the low growth rate of deep-sea prokaryotes, higher single-cell extracellular enzyme activity was detected [8], which is just the opposite of the prokaryotic characteristics of surface waters. For example, the single-cell alkaline phosphatase activity in the deep sea is significantly higher than that in the surface water, which seems incomprehensible, because the deep water has a high phosphate concentration, and the metabolism of deep-sea micro organisms should not be limited by phosphate. However, studies suggest that the high alkaline phosphatase activity in the deep sea is precisely a strategy for obtaining organic carbon from low-activity organic matter, not for obtaining phosphate[9]. It can be seen that the ability of deep-sea micro-organisms to utilize low-activity organic matter is significantly higher than that of upper-sea micro-organisms. Existing studies have also confirmed that the absorption ratio of D-type (low activity)/L-type (high activity) amino acids by prokaryotic communities increases significantly with depth [10, 11]. The deep sea spring archaea taxa are the main contributors. Compared with the low activity of deep-sea dissolved organic matter, the activity of colloidal and particulate matter (POM) that sinks from the euphotic zone to the deep-sea interior at different rates is relatively high. Therefore, deep-sea POM is crucial to the metabolism and distribution patterns of deep-sea micro organisms. Existing studies have also confirmed the life mode of deep-sea prokaryotes that are good at surface adsorption and their heterogeneous distribution around "hotspots" in the deep sea[5]. However, due to the easily decomposed characteristics of debris particles and their random distribution characteristics, it is still difficult to accurately study them with current sampling techniques. Archaeal metabolic pathways in deep-sea springs Prokaryotic communities are markedly stratified in the vertical oceanic water column. As the contribution of Bacteria to the total prokaryotic abundance gradually decreases with depth, the abundance of Archaea, especially Crenarchaeota, gradually increases with depth, and is one of the most abundant micro organisms in the deep sea. The total amount may account for 1/3 of the total prokaryotes in the global ocean [12]. Therefore, it plays an important role in the biogeochemical cycle of marine biogenic elements. However, the metabolic and functional roles of deep spring archaea are still controversial. Experimental studies of a cultured strain of Crynarchaea revealed that a major group of Crynarchaea plays a central role in the oceanic nitrogen cycle as they perform the critical first step in the conversion of ammonia-nitrogen to nitrate-nitrogen (ammonia oxidation). This finding is quite surprising, since ammonia oxidation has been thought to be performed by specific groups of bacteria for hundreds of years. At the same time, this kind of Cranearchaea also uses the energy provided by ammonia oxidation to fix inorganic carbon for autotrophic growth and metabolism. It can be seen that it also has a non-negligible position in the ocean carbon cycle. However, further studies of functional genes in natural waters revealed the diversity and complexity of the processes involved. Due to the relatively low ammonia concentration in the deep sea, the ammonia oxidation process may not be an important source of energy[13], which suggests that the metabolism of Crenararchaea in the deep sea may be dominated by heterotrophic metabolism. Nevertheless, the ability of Cryoarchaea to fix CO2 in oxygenated deep-sea water still highlights its important position in the deep-sea carbon cycle. Studies have estimated the amount of “dark CO2 fixation” in deep sea water to be about 1 mmol C/(m2.d)[10]. This is obviously a supplement to the deep-sea organic carbon pool that cannot be ignored; it also provides a source of new productivity of deep-sea organic matter. Therefore, this part of "dark CO2 fixation" is also considered as the "primary productivity" of the dark ocean. But the ability and extent of this part of the "primary productivity" to drive the deep-sea food web remains to be studied. Prospects Recent studies have shown that deep-sea prokaryotic biomass accounts for 75% of the global ocean total, and deep-sea prokaryotic productivity accounts for 50% of the global ocean total (Figure 1). Therefore, understanding the function of deep-sea microbiomes is crucial to understanding marine biogeochemical cycles, resource and environmental issues, and even global changes. Figure 1 	(a) prokaryotic biomass and (b) prokaryotic heterotrophic productivity of the three-section vertical water column integration (±SE, X upper axis, histogram), and the percentage of the three-section water column integration value to the total water column integration value (bar diagram Inner values)[5,14] More extensive deep-sea sampling surveys and the application of new technologies, such as (macro)genomics, (macro)transcriptomics, gene chip technology, etc., will reveal more unique features of prokaryotes. Metabolic pathways allow us to gain a new understanding of the function of deep-sea planktonic prokaryotic communities and their interactions (such as interactions with protists and viruses). Finally, the contradiction between the geochemical evidence and the measured value of the mineralization rate of organic matter in the ocean should be resolved [8]; the biogeographic distribution of the microbiome and the cycle of major elements in the ocean should be better connected, so as to achieve the understanding of the microfood cycle in different oceans. Mechanistic understanding of the field; better understanding of the impact of deep-sea microbiological processes on the ocean carbon cycle and global change.

question:
OSPF proposals offer equivalent connectivity/capacity. Share backbone/area-border roles if OSPF permits; otherwise split. Border connections join Area 0 to another area.
R: flood-prone river trade hub; 1 shared-role candidate, 2 backbone-only.
H: less-exposed upland, trade-remote; 2 shared-role candidates only.
Rate site/situation solely on flood exposure/trade access.
$000: router 20 now; annual maintenance 10/deployment; outage-year loss 100; annual benefits good/poor situation 125/90.
Wet/dry partition probabilities: 0.2/0.8.
Conditional outage probabilities (wet/dry): poor site 0.75/0.25; good site 0.2/0.
Two year-end cash flows; annual discount 10%; no other costs/salvage.
Which deployment maximizes expected NPV, by what margin (nearest $0.01 thousand)?
explanation: Site describes physical characteristics, while situation describes relationships with surrounding areas. Under the stated rating boundaries, R's flood exposure gives it a poor site, and its trade connections give it a good situation. H has a good site and poor situation. These classifications select R's annual benefit of 125 and conditional outage probabilities of 0.75/0.25, versus H's benefit of 90 and probabilities of 0.2/0. A backbone router may also serve as an area border router, so the proposed sharing is permitted. R therefore requires three physical routers costing 60, and H requires two costing 40. All amounts are in thousands of dollars. The law of total probability gives annual outage probabilities of 0.2 × 0.75 + 0.8 × 0.25 = 0.35 for R and 0.2 × 0.2 + 0.8 × 0 = 0.04 for H. Expected annual net cash flows are 125 − 10 − 35 = 80 and 90 − 10 − 4 = 76. The two-year present-value factor is 1/1.1 + 1/1.1² = 210/121. NPVs are 80 × 210/121 − 60 = 78.842975 for R and 76 × 210/121 − 40 = 91.900826 for H. H wins by 13.057851, or $13.06 thousand. R's favorable trade situation does not eliminate its physical flood disadvantage.

distractor_analysis.reason: Mistaking R's favorable trade situation for protection from its flood-exposed physical site leads to omitting R's outage losses while retaining H's losses -> R's annual net cash flow becomes 115 and its NPV becomes 139.586777, versus H's unchanged 91.900826 -> R, by $47.69 thousand.

Correctly classifying site/situation, counting routers, and calculating outage probabilities but keeping risk separate from valuation omits both expected outage losses -> annual net cash flows become 115 for R and 80 for H, producing NPVs of 139.586777 and 98.842975 -> R, by $40.74 thousand.

Incorrectly treating backbone and area-border roles as mutually exclusive triggers splitting every shared-role candidate into two physical devices -> both deployments are charged for four routers, costing 80 each; with correct risk-adjusted cash flows their NPVs become 58.842975 and 51.900826 -> R, by $6.94 thousand.

sample.prompt:
question:
Metabolic pathways and their environmental effects in deep-sea microbiomes
answer:
sample.completion: The so-called deep sea mainly refers to the water body below 1000m, which is characterized by no light, high pressure and low temperature. For a long time in the past, the dark deep ocean was generally considered to have almost negligible biologically active metabolism due to the harsh environmental conditions [1]. However, later studies have shown that this huge space covering 2/3 of our planet is filled with various micro organisms, carrying various life metabolic processes of micro organisms [2], and is the main place for the mineralization of organic matter in the ocean. Therefore, understanding the function of deep-sea microbiomes is critical to understanding global biogeochemical cycles. Deep-sea microfood rings and deep-sea microbiological characteristics Due to the lack of photosynthetic phytoplankton as the main food source of the food chain, the deep ocean has a food web structure and function that is completely different from that of the upper photonic ocean. The deep-sea food web structure is relatively simple, and the lack of this part of the function carried by phytoplankton is compensated by the metabolism of deep-sea prokaryotic autotrophs. At the same time, due to the decline in the availability of organic carbon in the deep sea, the entire microbiome is mainly regulated by the downward effect (availability of organic carbon). Therefore, adapting to the deep-sea environment and the characteristics of the deep-sea microfood ring, the deep-sea prokaryotic community also exhibits characteristics different from those of the euphotic prokaryotes: ①The nucleotide content of single cells is higher, which means that the genome of deep-sea cells is much larger than that of surface cells. Large genome, which implies that deep-sea micro organisms are good at "opportunistic" life mode[3]; ②Most deep-sea prokaryotes lack the expression gene of photolyase; ③Compared with the upper water body, more living organisms attach to the surface Pattern-related genes can be detected in the deep sea, which indicates that the metabolic activity of deep-sea prokaryotes may be related to particulate matter[4]. An important carrier on which metabolism depends. Deep-sea organic matter characteristics and microbial metabolism The deep-sea dissolved organic carbon (DOC) pool is mainly derived from biological processes in the upper ocean. Organic carbon is passed down through the vertical transport of particulate matter, the migration and transport of plankton, and the sedimentation and diffusion of water masses [5]. As the depth increases, the remineralization process of organic matter by micro organisms causes the continuous depletion of nitrogen (DON) and phosphorus (DOP) in dissolved organic matter (DOM), which leads to a significant increase in the ratio of deep-sea DOC:DON:DOP[6 ]. Therefore, the organic matter remineralization and degradation products of micro-organisms—high-carbon and low-molecular-weight dissolved organic matter constitute the deep-sea DOM pool. This characteristic determines the low activity of deep-sea organic carbon, so deep-sea prokaryotes have a relatively low growth rate compared with surface organisms [7]. However, the unique deep-sea environmental characteristics have created unique adaptation mechanisms for deep-sea micro-organisms. Accompanied by the low growth rate of deep-sea prokaryotes, higher single-cell extracellular enzyme activity was detected [8], which is just the opposite of the prokaryotic characteristics of surface waters. For example, the single-cell alkaline phosphatase activity in the deep sea is significantly higher than that in the surface water, which seems incomprehensible, because the deep water has a high phosphate concentration, and the metabolism of deep-sea micro organisms should not be limited by phosphate. However, studies suggest that the high alkaline phosphatase activity in the deep sea is precisely a strategy for obtaining organic carbon from low-activity organic matter, not for obtaining phosphate[9]. It can be seen that the ability of deep-sea micro-organisms to utilize low-activity organic matter is significantly higher than that of upper-sea micro-organisms. Existing studies have also confirmed that the absorption ratio of D-type (low activity)/L-type (high activity) amino acids by prokaryotic communities increases significantly with depth [10, 11]. The deep sea spring archaea taxa are the main contributors. Compared with the low activity of deep-sea dissolved organic matter, the activity of colloidal and particulate matter (POM) that sinks from the euphotic zone to the deep-sea interior at different rates is relatively high. Therefore, deep-sea POM is crucial to the metabolism and distribution patterns of deep-sea micro organisms. Existing studies have also confirmed the life mode of deep-sea prokaryotes that are good at surface adsorption and their heterogeneous distribution around "hotspots" in the deep sea[5]. However, due to the easily decomposed characteristics of debris particles and their random distribution characteristics, it is still difficult to accurately study them with current sampling techniques. Archaeal metabolic pathways in deep-sea springs Prokaryotic communities are markedly stratified in the vertical oceanic water column. As the contribution of Bacteria to the total prokaryotic abundance gradually decreases with depth, the abundance of Archaea, especially Crenarchaeota, gradually increases with depth, and is one of the most abundant micro organisms in the deep sea. The total amount may account for 1/3 of the total prokaryotes in the global ocean [12]. Therefore, it plays an important role in the biogeochemical cycle of marine biogenic elements. However, the metabolic and functional roles of deep spring archaea are still controversial. Experimental studies of a cultured strain of Crynarchaea revealed that a major group of Crynarchaea plays a central role in the oceanic nitrogen cycle as they perform the critical first step in the conversion of ammonia-nitrogen to nitrate-nitrogen (ammonia oxidation). This finding is quite surprising, since ammonia oxidation has been thought to be performed by specific groups of bacteria for hundreds of years. At the same time, this kind of Cranearchaea also uses the energy provided by ammonia oxidation to fix inorganic carbon for autotrophic growth and metabolism. It can be seen that it also has a non-negligible position in the ocean carbon cycle. However, further studies of functional genes in natural waters revealed the diversity and complexity of the processes involved. Due to the relatively low ammonia concentration in the deep sea, the ammonia oxidation process may not be an important source of energy[13], which suggests that the metabolism of Crenararchaea in the deep sea may be dominated by heterotrophic metabolism. Nevertheless, the ability of Cryoarchaea to fix CO2 in oxygenated deep-sea water still highlights its important position in the deep-sea carbon cycle. Studies have estimated the amount of “dark CO2 fixation” in deep sea water to be about 1 mmol C/(m2.d)[10]. This is obviously a supplement to the deep-sea organic carbon pool that cannot be ignored; it also provides a source of new productivity of deep-sea organic matter. Therefore, this part of "dark CO2 fixation" is also considered as the "primary productivity" of the dark ocean. But the ability and extent of this part of the "primary productivity" to drive the deep-sea food web remains to be studied. Prospects Recent studies have shown that deep-sea prokaryotic biomass accounts for 75% of the global ocean total, and deep-sea prokaryotic productivity accounts for 50% of the global ocean total (Figure 1). Therefore, understanding the function of deep-sea microbiomes is crucial to understanding marine biogeochemical cycles, resource and environmental issues, and even global changes. Figure 1 	(a) prokaryotic biomass and (b) prokaryotic heterotrophic productivity of the three-section vertical water column integration (±SE, X upper axis, histogram), and the percentage of the three-section water column integration value to the total water column integration value (bar diagram Inner values)[5,14] More extensive deep-sea sampling surveys and the application of new technologies, such as (macro)genomics, (macro)transcriptomics, gene chip technology, etc., will reveal more unique features of prokaryotes. Metabolic pathways allow us to gain a new understanding of the function of deep-sea planktonic prokaryotic communities and their interactions (such as interactions with protists and viruses). Finally, the contradiction between the geochemical evidence and the measured value of the mineralization rate of organic matter in the ocean should be resolved [8]; the biogeographic distribution of the microbiome and the cycle of major elements in the ocean should be better connected, so as to achieve the understanding of the microfood cycle in different oceans. Mechanistic understanding of the field; better understanding of the impact of deep-sea microbiological processes on the ocean carbon cycle and global change.

question:
A federal agency’s retention audit applies §552a(e)(7); other requirements hold. Next period’s 12 First-Amendment-activity records comprise disjoint groups: 5 expressly statute-authorized; 4 expressly subject-authorized; 2 pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law-enforcement activity; 1 with neither authorization nor law-enforcement connection. Currently 10 are eligible. Each eligible-record subset, including empty, gets one metadata-only configuration entry. Priorities are distinct, ascending; runtimes scale exactly with standard asymptotic work.

Service: seconds at 1,024 entries; fixed yuan; yuan/second
Straight insertion: 10; 100; 2
Nonadaptive merge: 10; 0; 5
First-element-pivot quicksort: 5; 0; 6

Excluding common costs, which service minimizes next-period budget?
explanation: Section 552a(e)(7) prohibits maintaining records describing individuals’ exercise of First Amendment rights unless expressly authorized by statute or the subject, or pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law-enforcement activity. Thus 5 + 4 + 2 = 11 records are eligible; the remaining record is excluded. The configuration workload increases from 2^10 = 1,024 to 2^11 = 2,048 entries, including the empty subset. Ascending distinct priorities have zero inversions, a special case of O(M) inversions. Straight insertion sort therefore has O(M) work, nonadaptive merge sort has O(M log₂ M) work, and first-element-pivot quicksort has O(M²) work because its partitions are maximally unbalanced. Under exact proportional scaling, their runtime multipliers are respectively 2, (2,048 × 11)/(1,024 × 10) = 2.2, and 4. Projected runtimes are 20, 22, and 20 seconds. Fixed fees remain unchanged, so projected budgets are 100 + 2 × 20 = 140 yuan, 0 + 5 × 22 = 110 yuan, and 0 + 6 × 20 = 120 yuan. Merge sort has the lowest next-period budget.

distractor_analysis.reason: Ignoring §552a(e)(7) and admitting all 12 proposed records -> 4,096 configurations, runtime multipliers of 4, 4.8, and 16, and budgets of 180, 240, and 480 yuan -> 'Insertion sort: 180 yuan'.

Calculating the correct projected budgets but choosing by the current-period bills of 120, 50, and 30 yuan -> selecting quicksort despite its next-period 120-yuan budget exceeding merge sort’s 110 yuan -> 'Quicksort: 120 yuan'.

Finding 11 eligible records and 2,048 configurations but applying runtime growth to records rather than entries -> multipliers of 1.1, (11 log₂ 11)/(10 log₂ 10) ≈ 1.14553, and 1.21, producing budgets of 122, approximately 57.28, and 36.30 yuan -> 'Quicksort: 36.30 yuan'.

question:
A federal agency applies 5 U.S.C. §552a(e)(7); other legal requirements hold. Next-period First-Amendment-activity records have disjoint grounds: 5 expressly statute-authorized, 4 expressly subject-authorized, 2 pertinent to and within authorized law-enforcement activity, 1 with none of these grounds.
Each eligible-record subset, including empty, yields one metadata-only entry; currently 10 records qualify. For M entries, inversions are O(M); first-element-pivot quicksort encounters worst-case partitions. Runtime scales exactly with leading asymptotic work.
Unchanged pricing; current (seconds, fixed yuan, yuan/second): straight insertion (10, 100, 2); merge (10, 0, 5); quicksort (5, 0, 6).
Excluding common costs, which service minimizes next-period spending, and at what budget?
explanation: Section 552a(e)(7) prohibits federal agencies from maintaining records describing individuals’ exercise of First Amendment rights unless expressly authorized by statute or by the individual, or pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law-enforcement activity. Thus 5 + 4 + 2 = 11 records qualify, while the remaining record does not. Including the empty subset, the configuration count increases from 2^10 = 1024 to 2^11 = 2048. Straight insertion sort with O(M) inversions takes O(M); merge sort takes O(M log₂ M); first-element-pivot quicksort under the stipulated worst-case partitions takes O(M²). Exact runtime scaling gives multipliers of 2, (2048 × 11)/(1024 × 10) = 2.2, and 4, respectively. Projected runtimes are 20, 22, and 20 seconds. Each budget is its unchanged fixed fee plus its per-second rate times projected runtime: insertion costs 100 + 2 × 20 = 140 yuan; merge costs 0 + 5 × 22 = 110 yuan; quicksort costs 0 + 6 × 20 = 120 yuan. Merge sort therefore minimizes next-period spending at 110 yuan.

semantic_audit.solution_summary: Section 552a(e)(7) permits the three stated exception categories, so 11 next-period records qualify. The entry count rises from 2^10 to 2^11. With linear insertion-sort work, M log₂ M merge-sort work, and quadratic worst-case quicksort work, runtimes become 20, 22, and 20 seconds respectively. Fixed-plus-variable spending is therefore 140, 110, and 120 yuan. Merge sort minimizes spending at 110 yuan.

computer_science.reason: Insertion sort with O(M) inversions has linear work; merge sort has M log M work; worst-case quicksort has quadratic work. Without these algorithmic relationships, the next-period runtimes cannot be determined.

mathematics.reason: An n-record set has 2^n subsets, including empty. Subset counting and scaling ratios determine the workload increase and runtime multipliers; treating record counts as entry counts gives incorrect budgets.

financial.reason: Service spending combines an unchanged fixed charge with runtime multiplied by the per-second rate. This budgeting relationship and comparison of total costs are necessary; runtime or variable cost alone does not establish the cheapest service.

legal.reason: Section 552a(e)(7) recognizes statute authorization, subject authorization, and pertinence within authorized law-enforcement activity as alternative exceptions. Applying those exceptions admits 11 records and excludes the remaining record. Without that rule, the eligible-record count and downstream budgets are undetermined.

question_plan: Ask which sorting service has the lowest next-period processing budget for a federal agency's retention-configuration audit tool. Apply the quoted Section 552a(e)(7) restriction, assuming all other legal requirements are satisfied. Of 12 proposed records describing individuals' First Amendment activities, five have express statutory authorization, four have express authorization from their subjects, two are stipulated to be pertinent to and within an authorized law-enforcement activity, and one meets no exception; these groups are disjoint. The tool creates one metadata-only configuration entry for every subset of eligible records, including the empty subset, and sorts those entries by priority. The current period has 10 eligible records. Specify nearly ordered configuration entries with O(M) inversions and quadratic behavior for the stated first-element-pivot quicksort. Model sorting runtime as exactly proportional to M, M log2 M, and M² for insertion sort, merge sort, and quicksort. At M = 1024, their measured runtimes are respectively 10, 10, and 5 seconds; their fixed fees are 100, 0, and 0 yuan, and runtime charges are 2, 5, and 6 yuan per second. All other tool costs are common and excluded. Require the eligible-record count, configuration count, runtime complexity and growth for each service, projected budgets, and cheapest next-period service.

answer_plans.plan: Exclude the record meeting no statutory exception, leaving 11 eligible records. Count 2^11 = 2048 configurations, versus 2^10 = 1024 currently. Use O(M), O(M log M), and O(M²), with runtime multipliers 2, 2.2, and 4. Project runtimes of 20, 22, and 20 seconds. Apply fixed fee plus rate times runtime to obtain 140, 110, and 120 yuan. Select merge sort at 110 yuan.

Ignore the retention restriction and include all 12 proposed records. Count 4096 configurations and correctly apply growth factors of 4, 4.8, and 16 relative to 1024. Compute budgets of 180, 240, and 480 yuan and incorrectly select insertion sort because the legally ineligible record inflated the configuration space.

Correctly identify 11 eligible records, 2048 configurations, all three sorting complexities, and projected budgets of 140, 110, and 120 yuan. Nevertheless, select quicksort using its lowest current-period bill of 30 yuan rather than integrating the projected workload and costs into the decision.

Correctly identify 11 eligible records and state that they yield 2048 configurations, but incorrectly apply sorting growth to the eligible-record increase from 10 to 11 rather than to the configuration increase from 1024 to 2048. Use factors 1.1, approximately 1.146, and 1.21, producing budgets of 122, approximately 57.28, and 36.30 yuan, and wrongly select quicksort.

mathematics.necessity: Convert n eligible records into 2^n configuration entries, the actual sorting workload.
Count the retain-nothing configuration rather than subtracting one from the workload.
Establish that increasing the eligible inventory from 10 to 11 doubles the configuration count.

financial.necessity: Keep each service's fixed fee unchanged when its sorting runtime grows.
Calculate runtime-dependent spending by multiplying projected seconds by the quoted per-second rate.
Add fixed and variable components using the charged activity, rather than scaling the whole bill or charging directly per record.

legal.necessity: Exclude the First Amendment activity record that meets none of the quoted statutory exceptions.
Include the five expressly statute-authorized records and four expressly subject-authorized records.
Include the two records stipulated to be pertinent to and within an authorized law-enforcement activity.

question:
A federal agency’s audit tool applies 5 U.S.C. §552a(e)(7); other legal requirements hold. Next-period First-Amendment-activity records, disjoint: 5 expressly statute-authorized; 4 expressly subject-authorized; 2 pertinent to and within authorized law-enforcement scope; 1 with neither authorization nor law-enforcement connection. Every eligible-record subset, including empty, generates one metadata-only entry; currently 10 records qualify. M entries have O(M) priority-order inversions; first-element-pivot quicksort makes worst-case partitions. Runtime scales exactly with leading operation-count terms.

Service: seconds at M=1024; fixed yuan; yuan/second
Straight insertion: 10; 100; 2
Merge: 10; 0; 5
Quicksort: 5; 0; 6

Excluding common costs, which service minimizes next-period spending, at what budget?
explanation: Section 552a(e)(7) prohibits maintaining records describing individuals’ First Amendment activities unless expressly authorized by statute or by the individuals concerned, or pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law-enforcement activity. Thus 5 + 4 + 2 = 11 records qualify; the remaining record does not. Including the empty subset gives 2^11 = 2048 configuration entries, compared with the current 2^10 = 1024. With O(M) inversions, straight insertion sort has O(M) runtime; merge sort has O(M log₂ M) runtime; the stipulated worst-case first-element-pivot quicksort has O(M²) runtime. Under the exact leading-term scaling model, the respective growth factors are 2, (2048 × 11)/(1024 × 10) = 2.2, and 4. Projected runtimes are 20, 22, and 20 seconds. Fixed fees plus runtime charges give budgets of 100 + 2 × 20 = 140 yuan, 0 + 5 × 22 = 110 yuan, and 0 + 6 × 20 = 120 yuan. Merge sort uniquely minimizes next-period spending at 110 yuan.

distractor_analysis.reason: Ignoring Section 552a(e)(7) and admitting all 12 proposed records -> 4096 entries, runtime growth factors of 4, 4.8, and 16, and projected budgets of 180, 240, and 480 yuan -> incorrectly selects straight insertion sort at 180 yuan.

Computing the correct next-period budgets but selecting by current-period spending -> quicksort’s current bill of 30 yuan beats merge sort’s 50 yuan and insertion sort’s 120 yuan, so the wrong service is chosen despite projected budgets of 140, 110, and 120 yuan -> reports quicksort with its projected budget of 120 yuan.

Recognizing 11 eligible records and 2048 configurations but applying sorting growth to the record count rather than the configuration count -> factors 11/10, (11 log₂11)/(10 log₂10), and (11/10)² yield budgets of 122, approximately 57.28, and 36.30 yuan -> incorrectly selects quicksort at 36.30 yuan.

semantic_audit.solution_summary: Cerebellar hemorrhage compressing the brainstem in this comatose, intubated patient calls for urgent neurosurgical management. Fiber provides the required electromagnetic-interference and noise immunity. The neurosurgery link requires 4 × 20 = 80 m of cable, giving an installed cost of 80 × 8 + 300 = 940 yuan, within the 1,000-yuan budget. A uses the wrong medium, D selects the wrong service, and B states an incorrect cost and funding decision.

computer_science.reason: Transmission-medium knowledge identifies fiber as satisfying the immunity requirement. Without it, the cheaper neurosurgery copper option cannot be excluded on technical grounds.

medical.reason: The clinical findings establish the need for urgent neurosurgical management rather than conservative ICU care. Without that knowledge, the affordable ICU fiber link remains a plausible alternative.

mathematics.reason: The square-perimeter relation determines the required 80 m of cable. Without it, the stated installed cost cannot be verified.

financial.reason: Fixed-versus-variable costing requires adding the installation charge once to the cable expenditure, then comparing total expenditure with the budget. Without that interpretation, the funding decision and installed total are not established by cable length alone.

question_plan: Construct a hospital capital-planning question reviewing the supplied case of coma with CT-confirmed cerebellar hemorrhage compressing the brainstem. Ask which destination, transmission medium, and installed-cost proposal should be funded to transmit images to the service needed for the appropriate immediate management. Make clear that this is retrospective infrastructure planning, not a reason to delay care. Require electromagnetic-interference and noise immunity. Stipulate that each proposed link uses a complete square-perimeter cable route: neurosurgery has a 20 m side, conservative-care ICU has a 15 m side, and interventional radiology has a 25 m side. Fiber costs 8 yuan per meter plus a fixed 300 yuan installation charge, with no additional cable or costs and a 1,000 yuan budget. Include copper alternatives and ask for one justified selection.

answer_plans.plan: The hemorrhage with brainstem compression requires neurosurgical consultation for emergency surgery, so choose the neurosurgery image link. Use fiber optics for electromagnetic-interference and noise immunity. Its full square route requires 4 × 20 = 80 m; the installed cost is 300 + 8 × 80 = 940 yuan, within the 1,000 yuan budget.

Choose the conservative-care ICU fiber link, correctly recognizing interference immunity and calculating 4 × 15 = 60 m and 300 + 8 × 60 = 780 yuan, but fail to recognize that the case calls for emergency neurosurgical consultation rather than conservative ICU management.

State that the patient needs emergency neurosurgical consultation, that fiber is interference-immune, and that the neurosurgery and ICU links cost 940 and 780 yuan respectively. Nevertheless, recommend the ICU fiber link solely because it is cheaper, leaving the clinical destination requirement disconnected from the procurement decision.

Identify neurosurgery and fiber correctly, but use the square's area, 20 × 20 = 400, as the billable cable length. Apply fixed-plus-variable costing to this incorrect quantity, report 3,500 yuan, and wrongly conclude that the clinically appropriate fiber link exceeds the budget.

Provides the critical CT finding supporting urgent intervention rather than conservative management.

Ensures the calculation uses boundary length rather than square area as the billable quantity.

Applies the sample's per-unit costing structure to cable price multiplied by installed meters.

question: Retrospective hospital planning—not a delay to care—reviews an intubated, comatose patient with CT-confirmed cerebellar hemorrhage compressing the brainstem. Images must reach the service required for immediate management, with electromagnetic-interference and noise immunity. Each cable route covers a complete square perimeter: neurosurgery side 20 m; conservative-care ICU 15 m; interventional radiology 25 m. Cost schedule: variable cable cost, fiber 8 yuan/m or copper 6 yuan/m; fixed installation cost, 300 yuan per link. There is no additional cable or cost. The budget is 1,000 yuan. Which proposal gives the required destination, medium, and correct total installed expenditure within budget?
explanation: Cerebellar hemorrhage with brainstem compression and coma requires emergency neurosurgical consultation and arrangements for surgery. The infrastructure destination is therefore neurosurgery. Fiber optics supplies electromagnetic-interference and noise immunity; copper does not. A complete square-perimeter route with side 20 m requires 4 × 20 = 80 m of cable, not the square's area of 400 m². Budgeted installed expenditure includes both the quantity-based variable cost and the fixed installation cost: 8 × 80 + 300 = 940 yuan, leaving 60 yuan within the budget. A is the only proposal satisfying all requirements. B has a correctly costed fiber link but the wrong clinical destination. C has a correctly costed neurosurgery link but the wrong medium. D has the correct destination and medium but reports only variable expenditure, not total installed expenditure.

distractor_analysis.reason: Treating conservative supportive ICU care as the appropriate immediate management despite brainstem compression selects the wrong service -> its 60 m fiber route correctly totals 300 + 8 × 60 = 780 yuan -> fund conservative-care ICU using fiber for 780 yuan.

Recognizing the neurosurgical destination and fiber's immunity separately but failing to apply immunity to procurement permits selection by lower price alone -> the neurosurgery copper link totals 300 + 6 × 80 = 780 yuan but fails the transmission requirement -> fund neurosurgery using copper for 780 yuan.

Misinterpreting the fixed installation cost as irrelevant to the link's budget because it does not vary with cable quantity excludes it from installed expenditure -> only 8 × 80 = 640 yuan is budgeted instead of 940 yuan -> fund neurosurgery using fiber at an understated total of 640 yuan.

question:
After oxygen, an unconscious 78-year-old has BP 70/35 mmHg, pulse 42/min. Protocol T: immediate transcutaneous pacing preparation; epinephrine/dopamine if unavailable. O: observe five minutes. Care never awaits alarms. Each fully backlogged ring rotates through 10 token hops and 10 frames. Hop/frame times h,f (ms) satisfy benchmarks (2h+f,2h+3f). Delivery adds 2 ms, processing 3 ms; alarm-latency limit: 40 ms. Dollars below: purchase now, maintenance only at two-year service end; annual discount 10%.
Package: protocol; benchmarks; purchase; maintenance
P: T; (4,8); 100; 121
Q: O; (3,5); 40; 60.50
R: T; (8,16); 50; 60.50
S: T; (4,8); 80; 181.50
Which eligible package minimizes present-value lifecycle cost?
explanation: Unconsciousness, severe hypotension, and bradycardia require the immediate response in protocol T, including epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable; observation excludes Q. Subtracting each first benchmark equation from the second gives 2f. Substitution then yields (h,f)=(1,2) for P and S, (1,1) for Q, and (2,4) for R, in milliseconds. Worst-case token access includes the entire rotation's token-passing and frame-transmission time: 10h+10f. Adding delivery and processing gives alarm latencies of 35, 25, 65, and 35 ms for P, Q, R, and S respectively. Thus only P and S satisfy both requirements. Present-value cost equals purchase plus maintenance/(1.10)^2. The respective costs are $200, $90, $100, and $230. P therefore minimizes present-value cost among eligible packages. Bedside treatment proceeds independently of alarm delivery.

distractor_analysis.reason: Treating observation as acceptable despite unstable symptomatic bradycardia leaves Q eligible because its latency is 25 ms -> its $90 present-value cost is lowest -> select Package Q.

Correctly identifying P and S as eligible and computing their present-value costs, but leaving those calculations disconnected from the final purchase-price ranking -> S wins on $80 upfront versus $100 despite costing $230 rather than $200 in present value -> select Package S.

Using half the full rotation as worst-case token access produces an erroneous R latency of (60/2)+5=35 ms -> R is incorrectly admitted and its $100 present-value cost beats the other medically suitable packages -> select Package R.

mathematics.necessity: The latency calculation must sum the specified full-ring components, separate alarm delivery time, and local clinical delays.

The selection must minimize lifecycle cost over deadline-compliant configurations rather than choose the fastest configuration.

financial.necessity: Each future maintenance payment must be converted to present value using its payment date and the specified discount rate.

Purchase cost and the present value of maintenance must be combined into the cost measure used to rank compliant configurations.

retrieval.query_instruction: Given a knowledge requirement, retrieve question-answer samples that provide the domain concepts, mechanisms, rules, or methods needed to satisfy it.

question: A 2-km² zone has arithmetic sensor density exactly 3; area units are km². All reports are ready: one single-segment report per nonempty subset of sensors that could fail. Upload immediately uses idealized slow start from a one-segment window, without losses or threshold crossing. Each round sends as many remaining reports as its window permits. RTT is 2 seconds; completion includes final acknowledgment and a full RTT for partial rounds. Tariff accounting data: fixed cost 16 yuan; variable rate 0.5 yuan; activity measure: upload seconds. Inclusive limits: 12 seconds, 22 yuan. What is the outcome (sensors, reports, rounds, seconds, yuan, meets both limits)?
explanation: Arithmetic density means item count divided by area, so the sensor count is 3 × 2 = 6. The six sensors form a set with 2^6 subsets. Excluding the empty subset gives 63 reports, each occupying one segment. Idealized slow start doubles the congestion window after each acknowledged round: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. These windows transmit 63 segments cumulatively in six rounds. With final acknowledgment included, duration is 6 × 2 = 12 seconds. Mixed-cost accounting includes the fixed component once and multiplies the variable rate by its activity quantity, elapsed upload seconds. Thus the charge is 16 + 0.5 × 12 = 22 yuan. Both inclusive limits are met exactly.

distractor_analysis.reason: Treat arithmetic density as the total count instead of recovering count from density and area -> 3 sensors produce 2^3 − 1 = 7 reports, requiring three rounds, 6 seconds, and 19 yuan -> (3, 7, 3, 6, 19, yes).

Calculate the correct transmission duration but fail to connect that duration to the tariff's activity measure, substituting report count for upload seconds -> 16 + 0.5 × 63 = 47.5 yuan incorrectly fails the budget test -> (6, 63, 6, 12, 47.5, no).

Require one congestion window to hold all reports instead of accumulating transmissions across rounds -> the first window accommodating 63 segments is 64 in round seven, implying 14 seconds and 23 yuan and failing both limits -> (6, 63, 7, 14, 23, no).

geography.prompt:
question:
Multilayer detachment tectonics of continental lithosphere
answer:
geography.completion:
Working model Decollement/detachment layer refers to a relatively weak rock-structure combination layer above the underlying rock combination, controlled by the overlying folded rock combination, and characterized by strong shear deformation. Multiple detachment layers may develop simultaneously or continuously during lithosphere deformation, and detachment layers may develop on different structural scales, so multi-layer detachment tectonics is the main mode of lithosphere deformation. The discovery of large-scale low-angle faults, such as extensional detachment faults[1,2] and large-scale low-angle thrust faults[3,4], has led structural geologists to propose that the continental lithosphere may be stratified according to physical properties . Therefore, when the lithosphere undergoes large-scale structural deformation, structural detachment may occur along the physical property mutation interface, forming a lithosphere-scale decollement fault. These detachment faults divide the lithosphere into structural layers with different petrophysical properties. Due to the different depths and temperature-pressure conditions of each structural layer, the deformation behavior of each structural layer is also different. A variety of hypothetical models have been proposed for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere. For example, in the Himalayas, southern Tibet, and other orogenic belts, under the thickening of the lithosphere, it is proposed that the middle-crust channel (or channel) flow model (mid-crustal ductile channel flow) to adjust the excess mass, which explains the phenomenon of the coexistence of surface extension and compression structures[5~7]. Jackson [8]'s continental lithosphere sandwich structure model (Fig. 1) uses the relationship between lithospheric rock physical conditions and temperature and pressure conditions to explain the reasons for the occurrence and existence of delamination structures. Evidence problem
Fig. 1 	Jackson lithosphere sandwich structure model [8] The lithosphere multi-layer detachment structure model has been supported by some field observations and experimental evidence, mainly including: ① Field observation support. Since the deformation traces of the deep structural layers of the lithosphere can be exposed under tectonic action, in some special structural parts, the structural traces formed by different structural layers of the lithosphere during the same tectonic process can "co-exist". A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). The above shows that multi-layer detachment tectonics can develop in different structural layers of lithosphere. Fig. 2. 	Three delaminated tectonic models in the formation of low-angle normal faults and metamorphic core complex structures[1,2] Brittle upper crust; 2. Ductile crust; 3. Lithospheric upper mantle; 4. Asthenosphere; 5. Magmatic rock② Evidence from deep geophysical exploration. The most important evidence support for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere comes from the results of deep geophysical exploration, including deep seismic reflection, magnetotelluric sounding, and Bouguer gravity anomaly detection. After the 5.12 Longmenshan Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008, Burchfiel et al. [11], based on data such as the Bouguer gravity anomaly, believed that the upper crust of Longmenshan did not thicken significantly, but the middle and lower crust with one to several layers of ductile flow crust was flowing eastward. In the process, it was blocked and thickened by the hard central Sichuan block under the Sichuan Basin, resulting in the vertical uplift of Longmenshan and the accumulation of abnormal stress, which eventually led to the Wenchuan earthquake in May 2008. This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. [11] further proves that the passage (or channel) flow mode [5~7]. In many mountain ranges, detachment faults have been recognized as one of the dominant factors of orogeny, such as the use of deep reflection seismic profiling (CORCOP) to discover a huge near-horizontal fault beneath the Blue Ridge of the Appalachians in the United States Thrust detachment zone, and pushed the Precambrian crystalline rock series of the Blue Ridge on the sedimentary cover of the Lower Paleozoic, and the thrust distance from the southeast to the northwest of the 5-15km thick foreign rock sheet Up to 260km[3, 4]. ③ Supported by experimental simulation results. In order to verify the multi-layer detachment structure model of the lithosphere, people use petrological and geochemical analysis methods, or carry out relevant high-temperature, high-pressure and petrological experimental analysis on rock samples at different structural levels, and on this basis put forward The delamination structural model of the lithosphere [12] better explains the deep structural detachment of the lithosphere. Figure 3 	Formation model of multi-layered detached nappe thin-skinned structures in the South China Yangtze block [6] Fz, Fc, Fs and Ft represent the structural detachment of the Sinian base, Cambrian base, Silurian and Triassic lower parts, respectively Some key scientific issues involved in the detachment surface[10] Although the multi-layer detachment structural model of the continental lithosphere has been supported by some observations and experimental evidence, there are still some key scientific issues that have not been resolved. Therefore, the multi-layer detachment structural model It is still a working hypothesis. These scientific issues mainly include: ① How to determine the interface properties of structural layer detachment? That is, what is the underground originality? For example, the physical properties and deformation behavior of the structural layer interface are the most critical issues in the deformation of multi-layer detachment structures. What we have observed in the field is the structural traces of the lithosphere exposed to the surface after multi-layer detachment and deformation. However, the interface inferred from deep geophysical data has multiple solutions. How to compare it with surface observations becomes a solution. the crux of the matter. Some researchers have also proposed to use high temperature and high pressure experiments to test. However, due to the limitation of the strain rate and boundary conditions such as temperature and pressure during the experiment, the current simulation is far from the actual environment of natural deformation. ② What is the deformation process of structural layer detachment? That is, what kind of deformation and metamorphism process has it experienced? When we observe on the surface, we invert the deformation process according to some structural kinematics pointing signs during the deformation. However, during the observation process, it was also found that many kinematic directions at the same time were inconsistent or even opposite. In addition, the deformation process we are inverting now does not limit the time and deformation rate, and even completely ignores the deformation process. Therefore, this inversion process may be very different from the natural process. ③ Reasons for deformation differences between structural layers? Among the different structural layers observed in the field, there are huge differences in deformation structural styles and combinations, as well as the metamorphic temperature-pressure conditions reflected by them, but the interface between the two layers, that is, the ductile detachment shear zone, may sometimes only be a few centimeters. What is the reason, what is the tectonic process, and the tectonic force can cause such a huge deformation-metamorphism difference between the upper and lower structural layers? ④ How big is the scale of delamination? Since the multi-layer detachment is based on the observation of low-angle faults, the change and extension scale/depth of low-angle faults are the most important basis for determining the scale of delamination. However, there is no research example so far that can accurately determine The occurrence change and scale of low-angle faults to the deep. Another question related to this is whether this kind of delamination structure only occurs in the middle and upper part of the lithosphere, or can it occur in the entire continental lithosphere? For example, is the delamination at the bottom of the lithosphere[12] a type of delamination tectonics? ⑤ Is there really a middle and lower crustal ductile channel flow in the middle and lower crust? Is it one layer or several layers? Is the multilayer detachment tectonics of the lithosphere controlled by the flow of these ductile flow shells? Or to what extent can the ductile flow crust control the deformation of the lithosphere? How to determine the nature of this fluid? There are no definitive answers to questions about the relative viscosities or rheology of fluids. Since the above key problems have not been resolved, traditional structural geology field observations are limited by surface rock outcrops, there are uncertainties and multi-solutions in the interpretation of deep geophysical detection data, and rock geochemical data have limitations in geological relationship analysis. Insufficient, especially the boundary conditions set by experimental structural geology are far from satisfying the physical, chemical and geological reality of the deep deformation of the continental lithosphere. Therefore, only by combining the studies of structural geology, geophysics and rock geochemistry, and realizing the complementary advantages of multiple disciplines, can objectively carry out more in-depth research on the multi-layer delamination structure of the lithosphere. With the continuous refinement of field structural analysis and the discovery of new important evidence and key structural phenomena, coupled with the continuous application of modern testing and simulation techniques in the field of earth sciences, the temperature-pressure conditions at different depths of the lithosphere and their Morphing features will gradually become a reality. On the basis of these studies, the continental lithosphere multi-layer delamination model will be continuously revised and improved.
