question:
Causes of large-scale marine organic matter accumulation events in geological history
answer:
geography.completion: Preface With the intensification of human activities, the nutrient salts (essential elements such as phosphorus, nitrogen, and silicon) input into rivers, lakes, and oceans have increased, causing eutrophication and algae blooms in aquatic ecosystems are very common. For example, the cyanobacteria pollution in Taihu Lake (Figure 1) and the red tides in the Yangtze River and Pearl River estuary that people talk about are all caused by changes in the nutrient salt mechanism in essence. In addition to human activities, continental weathering, upwelling, and submarine hydrothermal fluids are also important reasons for the increase in nutrients in some areas of the earth. In the superposition area of the above forces, the possibility of water body productivity increase is greater, for example, the coastal zone is often a high-value area of productivity. Figure 1 	Taihu Lake cyanobacteria pollution (network photo) None of the biogeochemical studies of modern marine nutrients can be used to describe the large-scale marine organic matter accumulation events that occurred on the earth in geological history. The existing evidence shows that when these events occurred, almost Eutrophication occurred in the whole ocean basin, which is not available on the modern earth. In the Phanerozoic, such events have occurred many times, Early Cambrian (concentrated at 542~521Ma), Late Ordovician/Early Silurian (concentrated at 445~439Ma), Late Devonian/Early Carboniferous (concentrated at 374-345Ma), Late Permian (concentrated at 260-251Ma), Late Triassic (concentrated at 228-203Ma), Late Jurassic (concentrated at 155-150Ma), Early Cretaceous (concentrated at 125-203Ma) 93Ma) and other periods, large-scale marine organic matter accumulation events occurred. The organic carbon content accumulated in the sediments can reach up to about 40% [1], such a high organic matter content is not available in today's marine sediments. The impact of these events on the Earth system is very profound. First, it changes the pattern of the carbon pool, so that a large part of carbon enters the sedimentary circle in the form of organic matter, and this part of carbon is mainly converted from atmospheric CO2 through photosynthesis, resulting in a sharp decline in atmospheric CO2 content, which is harmful to the earth. Revolutionary impact on surface climate and ecosystems. After the accumulation event, the climate is often dry and cold, and the biomass decreases sharply. Secondly, the large-scale accumulation of organic matter has fundamentally changed the chemical properties of ocean water. Water stratification and anaerobic, lower pH, and lower content of certain trace elements in water may lead to the collapse of aquatic ecosystems and the extinction of some organisms. . The impact of the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean during geological history on modern humans is that the fossil energy we rely on, oil, mainly comes from these deposits. The parent material of this type of organic matter is mainly algae, which is rich in lipids and forms more than 80% of today's crude oil. Understanding the causes of large-scale organic matter accumulation in the ocean is a major event in the study of Earth system science, but unfortunately, the current research at home and abroad is still at the level of data accumulation, and it is still far from the goal of fundamentally solving this problem. Far. Relevant research history, problem proposal and research difficulty There are quite a lot of scientific problems that can be explored in black rock series rich in organic matter and oil shale, which need to be studied by experts and scholars in different fields. For a long time in the past, our research are concentrated at this level. ① The nature and evolution of organic matter. Through the study of the types of organic matter [2, 3] and the structure of macromolecules in rocks, people have basically clarified the nature of organic matter in marine sediments. It is a complex organic matter mainly composed of lipid compounds [4], At different thermal evolution stages, the properties of organic matter vary greatly. In the highly mature stage, this type of organic matter is pyrolyzed and transformed into organic matter mainly with aromatic structure. ② Parent source of organic matter and water column process. The sedimentary marine organic matter inherited the stable composition of the marine biological organic matter. By comparing with the composition of the biological parent material, it is basically certain that it mainly comes from algal substances. The dominant algae species are not completely the same in different periods. In addition, marine organic matter comes from bacteria that decompose algae. The research on the parent source of sedimentary organic matter has greatly stimulated the research on the stable components of different biological organic matter and the research on the water column process after the death of biological organic matter. Today, we can use the knowledge accumulated by the predecessors to identify different biological parent materials from sedimentary organic matter. . ③ Reconstruction of water column biogeochemical processes. Accurate parent source and process identification technology allows us to reconstruct the paleobiogeochemical process of the water column from the study of sedimentary organic matter[5], solve the primary productivity of the water column, conduct detailed water column stratification and bacterial decomposition process research, etc.[6 ], which is a remarkable research result. From a large number of studies on the reconstruction of paleobiogeochemical processes, we will find that the formation process of sedimentary organic matter is very different in different periods, which stimulates people's research on the formation mechanism of sedimentary organic matter. In recent years, many excellent scholars in the world have linked this research with the carbon cycle process. For example, the large-scale accumulation of organic matter at the North Atlantic C/T boundary (93.6±0.8Ma) can reduce atmospheric CO2 by 80%[7 ], which is considered to be the reason for the cold and dry climate after C/T. This work also made many organic geochemists realize that the reason controlling the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean may be a special biogeochemical process, that is, a special enrichment mechanism of nutrients. How to find relevant evidence in geological bodies and connect them organically is a difficult problem in current research. The difficulty of research is firstly manifested as an interdisciplinary problem, which cannot be solved only by the research that organic geochemists are good at. The special nutrient supply mechanism involves issues such as the source and rapid generation of nutrient salt, and inorganic geochemical research is also required. home participation. The second difficulty is that although the research results of modern biogeochemistry can be used for reference in terms of mechanism, it is a study without modern examples after all, and it is difficult to implement the principles of present and ancient, which is also a major obstacle to quickly solve this problem . The third difficulty is that it is difficult to find the entry point of the research, and the existing technical route is not easy to implement. Studying this problem from sedimentary records is probably the best research method, but it only solves the problem of time series, and the spatial relationship of various elements of event occurrence still needs comprehensive regional research to solve. The possible reasons for the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean The large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean is attributed to high productivity and a good environment for preserving organic matter. Generally, organic matter is easy to oxidize, and the reducing environment is conducive to the preservation of organic matter[8]. It is very important for the preservation of organic matter in the case of low productivity. Under the condition of high productivity, due to the sufficient supply of organic matter, the bottom of the water body is always reduced. The reducing environment was not enough to be the main controlling factor, and high productivity became the decisive factor for high organic matter accumulation. High primary productivity requires special nutrient supply, and special nutrient supply requires special or extreme geological events. From this perspective, we can roughly guess the possible reasons for the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the Phanerozoic ocean. It is nothing more than the following three situation. The first mechanism is that volcanic activity provides nutrients. Volcanic activity occurs for a short period of time. As long as the area is large enough, volcanic ash can provide a large amount of nutrients after dissolution. The high organic matter accumulation in Late Devonian/Early Carboniferous (concentrated at 374-345Ma) and Early Cretaceous (concentrated at 125-93Ma) may be related to this. The second mechanism is the supply of nutrients after the large ice age. There is obvious physical weathering during the glacial period, but it is very difficult for these substances to be transported to the ocean due to the consolidation of ice. In the late glacial period, these nutrients enter the ocean in a short period of time, which can cause eutrophication, thereby leading to the accumulation of organic matter. . The Precambrian Marino and Stuart glacial periods and the Late Ordovician/Early Silurian (concentrated at 445-439Ma) glacial periods are very likely to provide nutrients for the subsequent large-scale accumulation of organic matter. The third mechanism is the supply of nutrients after extreme drought. Physical weathering under arid conditions has resulted in the accumulation of nutrients on land, with the potential to enter the ocean on a large scale during later climate transition phases, thereby providing conditions for algal blooms. It is possible that the high organic matter layers in Paleogene lakes in eastern China were formed in this way. The above three situations are special nutrient supply caused by extreme conditions. For a specific layer, there may be multiple mechanisms coexisting. For example, volcanic activities may cool the climate and thus generate glaciers. The two may together play a role in the accumulation of organic matter. None of these three hypotheses have been verified by the sedimentary record and need to be worked hard in our future work. If terrestrial systems, especially the biosphere, are to be included in the study of sphere-level interactions, then what can link events in the inorganic world with the organic world? It can be said with certainty that the mechanism of nutrients is a very important link, and only by studying the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean from the perspective of biogeochemistry can we truly solve its mechanism.

question: A reference network has 600 devices across 30 km². A new 50-km² network must have the same arithmetic density. Each new device generates TCP segments at an integrable rate f(t), with 1,000 ≤ f(t) ≤ 2,000 segments/day throughout a 30-day month; integrating its rate over that month gives its segment count. The logger stores only each segment's TCP window size field, without compression or overhead. Archiving costs 40 yuan/month plus 0.5 yuan per decimal MB (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes). What are the tight monthly archive-cost bounds, and is a 90-yuan budget guaranteed sufficient?
explanation: Arithmetic density is the number of items per unit area. The reference density is 600/30 = 20 devices/km², so the new network has 20 × 50 = 1,000 devices. Integrating the rate bounds over 30 days gives 30,000–60,000 segments per device, hence 30–60 million segments across the network. The TCP window size field occupies 2 bytes, so the archived volume is 60–120 million bytes, or 60–120 decimal MB. Adding the fixed charge once gives costs from 40 + 0.5 × 60 = 70 yuan to 40 + 0.5 × 120 = 100 yuan. Both endpoints are attainable with constant rates at the corresponding limits, so these bounds are tight. Since the maximum exceeds 90 yuan, the budget is not guaranteed sufficient.

question:
Multilayer detachment tectonics of continental lithosphere
answer:
sample.completion:
Working model Decollement/detachment layer refers to a relatively weak rock-structure combination layer above the underlying rock combination, controlled by the overlying folded rock combination, and characterized by strong shear deformation. Multiple detachment layers may develop simultaneously or continuously during lithosphere deformation, and detachment layers may develop on different structural scales, so multi-layer detachment tectonics is the main mode of lithosphere deformation. The discovery of large-scale low-angle faults, such as extensional detachment faults[1,2] and large-scale low-angle thrust faults[3,4], has led structural geologists to propose that the continental lithosphere may be stratified according to physical properties . Therefore, when the lithosphere undergoes large-scale structural deformation, structural detachment may occur along the physical property mutation interface, forming a lithosphere-scale decollement fault. These detachment faults divide the lithosphere into structural layers with different petrophysical properties. Due to the different depths and temperature-pressure conditions of each structural layer, the deformation behavior of each structural layer is also different. A variety of hypothetical models have been proposed for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere. For example, in the Himalayas, southern Tibet, and other orogenic belts, under the thickening of the lithosphere, it is proposed that the middle-crust channel (or channel) flow model (mid-crustal ductile channel flow) to adjust the excess mass, which explains the phenomenon of the coexistence of surface extension and compression structures[5~7]. Jackson [8]'s continental lithosphere sandwich structure model (Fig. 1) uses the relationship between lithospheric rock physical conditions and temperature and pressure conditions to explain the reasons for the occurrence and existence of delamination structures. Evidence problem
Fig. 1 	Jackson lithosphere sandwich structure model [8] The lithosphere multi-layer detachment structure model has been supported by some field observations and experimental evidence, mainly including: ① Field observation support. Since the deformation traces of the deep structural layers of the lithosphere can be exposed under tectonic action, in some special structural parts, the structural traces formed by different structural layers of the lithosphere during the same tectonic process can "co-exist". A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). The above shows that multi-layer detachment tectonics can develop in different structural layers of lithosphere. Fig. 2. 	Three delaminated tectonic models in the formation of low-angle normal faults and metamorphic core complex structures[1,2] Brittle upper crust; 2. Ductile crust; 3. Lithospheric upper mantle; 4. Asthenosphere; 5. Magmatic rock② Evidence from deep geophysical exploration. The most important evidence support for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere comes from the results of deep geophysical exploration, including deep seismic reflection, magnetotelluric sounding, and Bouguer gravity anomaly detection. After the 5.12 Longmenshan Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008, Burchfiel et al. [11], based on data such as the Bouguer gravity anomaly, believed that the upper crust of Longmenshan did not thicken significantly, but the middle and lower crust with one to several layers of ductile flow crust was flowing eastward. In the process, it was blocked and thickened by the hard central Sichuan block under the Sichuan Basin, resulting in the vertical uplift of Longmenshan and the accumulation of abnormal stress, which eventually led to the Wenchuan earthquake in May 2008. This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. [11] further proves that the passage (or channel) flow mode [5~7]. In many mountain ranges, detachment faults have been recognized as one of the dominant factors of orogeny, such as the use of deep reflection seismic profiling (CORCOP) to discover a huge near-horizontal fault beneath the Blue Ridge of the Appalachians in the United States Thrust detachment zone, and pushed the Precambrian crystalline rock series of the Blue Ridge on the sedimentary cover of the Lower Paleozoic, and the thrust distance from the southeast to the northwest of the 5-15km thick foreign rock sheet Up to 260km[3, 4]. ③ Supported by experimental simulation results. In order to verify the multi-layer detachment structure model of the lithosphere, people use petrological and geochemical analysis methods, or carry out relevant high-temperature, high-pressure and petrological experimental analysis on rock samples at different structural levels, and on this basis put forward The delamination structural model of the lithosphere [12] better explains the deep structural detachment of the lithosphere. Figure 3 	Formation model of multi-layered detached nappe thin-skinned structures in the South China Yangtze block [6] Fz, Fc, Fs and Ft represent the structural detachment of the Sinian base, Cambrian base, Silurian and Triassic lower parts, respectively Some key scientific issues involved in the detachment surface[10] Although the multi-layer detachment structural model of the continental lithosphere has been supported by some observations and experimental evidence, there are still some key scientific issues that have not been resolved. Therefore, the multi-layer detachment structural model It is still a working hypothesis. These scientific issues mainly include: ① How to determine the interface properties of structural layer detachment? That is, what is the underground originality? For example, the physical properties and deformation behavior of the structural layer interface are the most critical issues in the deformation of multi-layer detachment structures. What we have observed in the field is the structural traces of the lithosphere exposed to the surface after multi-layer detachment and deformation. However, the interface inferred from deep geophysical data has multiple solutions. How to compare it with surface observations becomes a solution. the crux of the matter. Some researchers have also proposed to use high temperature and high pressure experiments to test. However, due to the limitation of the strain rate and boundary conditions such as temperature and pressure during the experiment, the current simulation is far from the actual environment of natural deformation. ② What is the deformation process of structural layer detachment? That is, what kind of deformation and metamorphism process has it experienced? When we observe on the surface, we invert the deformation process according to some structural kinematics pointing signs during the deformation. However, during the observation process, it was also found that many kinematic directions at the same time were inconsistent or even opposite. In addition, the deformation process we are inverting now does not limit the time and deformation rate, and even completely ignores the deformation process. Therefore, this inversion process may be very different from the natural process. ③ Reasons for deformation differences between structural layers? Among the different structural layers observed in the field, there are huge differences in deformation structural styles and combinations, as well as the metamorphic temperature-pressure conditions reflected by them, but the interface between the two layers, that is, the ductile detachment shear zone, may sometimes only be a few centimeters. What is the reason, what is the tectonic process, and the tectonic force can cause such a huge deformation-metamorphism difference between the upper and lower structural layers? ④ How big is the scale of delamination? Since the above key problems have not been resolved, traditional structural geology field observations are limited by surface rock outcrops, there are uncertainties and multi-solutions in the interpretation of deep geophysical detection data, and rock geochemical data have limitations in geological relationship analysis. Insufficient, especially the boundary conditions set by experimental structural geology are far from satisfying the physical, chemical and geological reality of the deep deformation of the continental lithosphere. Therefore, only by combining the studies of structural geology, geophysics and rock geochemistry, and realizing the complementary advantages of multiple disciplines, can objectively carry out more in-depth research on the multi-layer delamination structure of the lithosphere. With the continuous refinement of field structural analysis and the discovery of new important evidence and key structural phenomena, coupled with the continuous application of modern testing and simulation techniques in the field of earth sciences, the temperature-pressure conditions at different depths of the lithosphere and their Morphing features will gradually become a reality. question:
Causes of large-scale marine organic matter accumulation events in geological history
answer:
sample.completion: Preface With the intensification of human activities, the nutrient salts (essential elements such as phosphorus, nitrogen, and silicon) input into rivers, lakes, and oceans have increased, causing eutrophication and algae blooms in aquatic ecosystems are very common. For example, the cyanobacteria pollution in Taihu Lake (Figure 1) and the red tides in the Yangtze River and Pearl River estuary that people talk about are all caused by changes in the nutrient salt mechanism in essence. In addition to human activities, continental weathering, upwelling, and submarine hydrothermal fluids are also important reasons for the increase in nutrients in some areas of the earth. In the superposition area of the above forces, the possibility of water body productivity increase is greater, for example, the coastal zone is often a high-value area of productivity. Figure 1 	Taihu Lake cyanobacteria pollution (network photo) None of the biogeochemical studies of modern marine nutrients can be used to describe the large-scale marine organic matter accumulation events that occurred on the earth in geological history. The existing evidence shows that when these events occurred, almost Eutrophication occurred in the whole ocean basin, which is not available on the modern earth. In the Phanerozoic, such events have occurred many times, Early Cambrian (concentrated at 542~521Ma), Late Ordovician/Early Silurian (concentrated at 445~439Ma), Late Devonian/Early Carboniferous (concentrated at 374-345Ma), Late Permian (concentrated at 260-251Ma), Late Triassic (concentrated at 228-203Ma), Late Jurassic (concentrated at 155-150Ma), Early Cretaceous (concentrated at 125-203Ma) 93Ma) and other periods, large-scale marine organic matter accumulation events occurred. The organic carbon content accumulated in the sediments can reach up to about 40% [1], such a high organic matter content is not available in today's marine sediments. The impact of these events on the Earth system is very profound. First, it changes the pattern of the carbon pool, so that a large part of carbon enters the sedimentary circle in the form of organic matter, and this part of carbon is mainly converted from atmospheric CO2 through photosynthesis, resulting in a sharp decline in atmospheric CO2 content, which is harmful to the earth. Revolutionary impact on surface climate and ecosystems. After the accumulation event, the climate is often dry and cold, and the biomass decreases sharply. Secondly, the large-scale accumulation of organic matter has fundamentally changed the chemical properties of ocean water. Water stratification and anaerobic, lower pH, and lower content of certain trace elements in water may lead to the collapse of aquatic ecosystems and the extinction of some organisms. . The impact of the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean during geological history on modern humans is that the fossil energy we rely on, oil, mainly comes from these deposits. The parent material of this type of organic matter is mainly algae, which is rich in lipids and forms more than 80% of today's crude oil. Understanding the causes of large-scale organic matter accumulation in the ocean is a major event in the study of Earth system science, but unfortunately, the current research at home and abroad is still at the level of data accumulation, and it is still far from the goal of fundamentally solving this problem. Far. Relevant research history, problem proposal and research difficulty There are quite a lot of scientific problems that can be explored in black rock series rich in organic matter and oil shale, which need to be studied by experts and scholars in different fields. For a long time in the past, our research are concentrated at this level. ① The nature and evolution of organic matter. Through the study of the types of organic matter [2, 3] and the structure of macromolecules in rocks, people have basically clarified the nature of organic matter in marine sediments. It is a complex organic matter mainly composed of lipid compounds [4], At different thermal evolution stages, the properties of organic matter vary greatly. In the highly mature stage, this type of organic matter is pyrolyzed and transformed into organic matter mainly with aromatic structure. ② Parent source of organic matter and water column process. The sedimentary marine organic matter inherited the stable composition of the marine biological organic matter. By comparing with the composition of the biological parent material, it is basically certain that it mainly comes from algal substances. The dominant algae species are not completely the same in different periods. In addition, marine organic matter comes from bacteria that decompose algae. The research on the parent source of sedimentary organic matter has greatly stimulated the research on the stable components of different biological organic matter and the research on the water column process after the death of biological organic matter. Today, we can use the knowledge accumulated by the predecessors to identify different biological parent materials from sedimentary organic matter. . ③ Reconstruction of water column biogeochemical processes. Accurate parent source and process identification technology allows us to reconstruct the paleobiogeochemical process of the water column from the study of sedimentary organic matter[5], solve the primary productivity of the water column, conduct detailed water column stratification and bacterial decomposition process research, etc.[6 ], which is a remarkable research result. From a large number of studies on the reconstruction of paleobiogeochemical processes, we will find that the formation process of sedimentary organic matter is very different in different periods, which stimulates people's research on the formation mechanism of sedimentary organic matter. In recent years, many excellent scholars in the world have linked this research with the carbon cycle process. For example, the large-scale accumulation of organic matter at the North Atlantic C/T boundary (93.6±0.8Ma) can reduce atmospheric CO2 by 80%[7 ], which is considered to be the reason for the cold and dry climate after C/T. This work also made many organic geochemists realize that the reason controlling the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean may be a special biogeochemical process, that is, a special enrichment mechanism of nutrients. How to find relevant evidence in geological bodies and connect them organically is a difficult problem in current research. The difficulty of research is firstly manifested as an interdisciplinary problem, which cannot be solved only by the research that organic geochemists are good at. The special nutrient supply mechanism involves issues such as the source and rapid generation of nutrient salt, and inorganic geochemical research is also required. home participation. The second difficulty is that although the research results of modern biogeochemistry can be used for reference in terms of mechanism, it is a study without modern examples after all, and it is difficult to implement the principles of present and ancient, which is also a major obstacle to quickly solve this problem . The third difficulty is that it is difficult to find the entry point of the research, and the existing technical route is not easy to implement. Studying this problem from sedimentary records is probably the best research method, but it only solves the problem of time series, and the spatial relationship of various elements of event occurrence still needs comprehensive regional research to solve. The possible reasons for the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean The large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean is attributed to high productivity and a good environment for preserving organic matter. Generally, organic matter is easy to oxidize, and the reducing environment is conducive to the preservation of organic matter[8]. It is very important for the preservation of organic matter in the case of low productivity. Under the condition of high productivity, due to the sufficient supply of organic matter, the bottom of the water body is always reduced. The reducing environment was not enough to be the main controlling factor, and high productivity became the decisive factor for high organic matter accumulation. High primary productivity requires special nutrient supply, and special nutrient supply requires special or extreme geological events. From this perspective, we can roughly guess the possible reasons for the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the Phanerozoic ocean. It is nothing more than the following three situation. The first mechanism is that volcanic activity provides nutrients. Volcanic activity occurs for a short period of time. As long as the area is large enough, volcanic ash can provide a large amount of nutrients after dissolution. The high organic matter accumulation in Late Devonian/Early Carboniferous (concentrated at 374-345Ma) and Early Cretaceous (concentrated at 125-93Ma) may be related to this. The second mechanism is the supply of nutrients after the large ice age. There is obvious physical weathering during the glacial period, but it is very difficult for these substances to be transported to the ocean due to the consolidation of ice. In the late glacial period, these nutrients enter the ocean in a short period of time, which can cause eutrophication, thereby leading to the accumulation of organic matter. . The Precambrian Marino and Stuart glacial periods and the Late Ordovician/Early Silurian (concentrated at 445-439Ma) glacial periods are very likely to provide nutrients for the subsequent large-scale accumulation of organic matter. The third mechanism is the supply of nutrients after extreme drought. Physical weathering under arid conditions has resulted in the accumulation of nutrients on land, with the potential to enter the ocean on a large scale during later climate transition phases, thereby providing conditions for algal blooms. It is possible that the high organic matter layers in Paleogene lakes in eastern China were formed in this way. The above three situations are special nutrient supply caused by extreme conditions. For a specific layer, there may be multiple mechanisms coexisting. For example, volcanic activities may cool the climate and thus generate glaciers. The two may together play a role in the accumulation of organic matter. None of these three hypotheses have been verified by the sedimentary record and need to be worked hard in our future work. If terrestrial systems, especially the biosphere, are to be included in the study of sphere-level interactions, then what can link events in the inorganic world with the organic world? It can be said with certainty that the mechanism of nutrients is a very important link, and only by studying the large-scale accumulation of organic matter in the ocean from the perspective of biogeochemistry can we truly solve its mechanism.

question:
Please calculate the unearned premium reserve as of 2009-12-31 for the following three one-year policies A, B, and C, each with a premium of 2000 yuan. The signing date of policy A is 2009-6-1, the signing date of policy B is 2008-7-1, and the signing date of policy C is 2007-6-10. According to the rule of seventy-eight, the result is ____.
options:
A.Less than 200
B.Greater than or equal to 200 and less than 250
C.Greater than or equal to 250 and less than 300
D.Greater than or equal to 300 and less than 350
answer:
financial.completion:
D.Greater than or equal to 300 and less than 350
explanation:
1. The valuation date for the unearned premium reserve, namely 2009-12-31, is 7 months from the inception date of policy A. At this time, policy B and policy C have already expired, so only the unearned premium reserve for policy A needs to be calculated. 2. From the rule of seventy-eight: the proportion of earned premium in the $i$-th month from the insurance inception date is $\frac{13-i}{78}$; therefore, the earned premium for policy A is $\sum_{i=1}^7\hat{p}_3=\frac{13-i}{78}=\frac{63}{78}$, and the proportion of the unearned premium reserve is $1-\frac{63}{78}=\frac{15}{78}$. Therefore, the unearned premium reserve is $\frac{15}{78}\times2000=384$, less than 200.

question:
A flood-insurance program reads logical file block 100: a flood-prone river city with profitable regional trade. Wet/dry years partition all years, with probabilities 0.25/0.75 and conditional flood probabilities 0.20/0.04, respectively. Annually: at most one flood; fixed payout 100,000 yuan; no other costs. Benchmark: expected annual claims. The proposed 6,000-yuan annual premium cites trade-implied safety and promotion.

Audit findings:
1. Reading requires the system-call interface.
2. Poor site, good situation; trade does not establish flood safety.
3. Annual risk is 8%; benchmark 8,000 yuan; premium inadequate.
4. Rate-setting principles include fairness/reasonableness, adequacy, promotion—not relative stability.

How many findings are correct?
explanation: Findings 1, 2, and 3 are correct; finding 4 is false. Programmatic access to the file block uses the operating system's system-call interface. The flood-prone physical location is a poor site, while profitable regional trade connections give it a good situation; those connections do not establish physical flood safety. Wet and dry years form a mutually exclusive, exhaustive partition, so annual flood probability is 0.25 × 0.20 + 0.75 × 0.04 = 0.08. With at most one flood and a fixed covered payout of 100,000 yuan, expected annual claims are 8,000 yuan. The 6,000-yuan annual premium is therefore inadequate under the stipulated benchmark. The applicable listed property-insurance rate-setting principles are fairness and reasonableness, adequacy, and relative stability, not promotion. Thus neither part of the program's proposed justification is sound, and exactly three findings are correct.

distractor_analysis.reason: Mistaking promotion for an applicable property-insurance rate-setting principle and excluding relative stability -> incorrectly accepting finding 4 alongside the three correct findings -> a count of 4.

Recognizing system calls, site versus situation, the total-probability formula, and the insurance principles separately without applying the formula and expected-claims benchmark to this record -> treating finding 3 as unestablished while accepting findings 1 and 2 and rejecting finding 4 -> a count of 2.

Treating the good trade situation as establishing flood safety and eliminating the wet-year risk contribution -> incorrectly rejecting finding 2 and calculating only 0.75 × 0.04 = 3%, a 3,000-yuan benchmark, and an adequate 6,000-yuan premium, thereby rejecting finding 3 as well -> accepting only finding 1 and reporting a count of 1.

original_plan.question_plan: Design a task asking which program workflow correctly estimates a property's expected annual flood-insurance payout from a north-up flood-probability raster. Supply the property's coordinates, raster origin and cell size, fixed bytes per cell, and block size; specify that each raster row occupies one file logical block, with no header, and choose coordinates placing the property in the 100th row. Provide the conditional flood damage and deductible, assuming no policy limit and at most one flood annually. Require coordinate-to-cell mapping, operating-system file access, and calculation of the expected payout from the retrieved probability.

answer_plans.plan: Map the coordinates to zero-based raster row 99 and column c, accounting for rows progressing southward. Use the operating system's system-call interface to read the probability at byte offset 99 times block size plus c times bytes per cell. Multiply that probability by the greater of conditional damage minus deductible and zero.
Correctly locate and read the property's flood probability through system calls, but multiply it by the full conditional damage without subtracting the insurance deductible.

State the correct geographic mapping, byte-offset formula, system-call interface, and deductible-adjusted expected-payout formula, but calculate the reported payout using the raster's overall mean probability rather than the probability retrieved for the property.

Correctly map the property to the 100th raster row, but translate that ordinal into byte offset 100 times block size plus the column displacement instead of using row index 99. Apply the correct insurance formula to the probability read from the wrong row.

mathematics.necessity: The 100th row corresponds to index 99, distinguishing the correct displacement from the off-by-one alternative.
Multiplying each index by its stride and adding gives 99 times block size plus column index times bytes per cell.
Weighting the flood payout by its probability and the zero nonflood payout by its complementary probability yields the expected annual payout.

geography.necessity: Raster rows progress southward, so row identification must account for decreasing northing.
The property's coordinates, raster origin, and cell dimensions determine its containing row and column.
The estimate must use the probability at the property's location rather than the raster-wide mean.

financial.necessity: The flood payout is the greater of conditional damage minus the deductible and zero, not the full damage.
The absence of a policy limit means no upper cap is applied to the deductible-adjusted payout.
At most one flood annually makes the year's total insurance payment equal to the sole flood claim payment or zero.

question: A monitor uniformly samples 1,000 m³ of air over one day, collecting all NaOH into 1 cL of final solution: 16% NaOH by mass, density 1.18 g/cm³, NaOH molar mass 40 g/mol. Fictional daily/hourly limits are 2 × 10^-5 and 6 × 10^-5 mol/m³, unordered; use the usual long-/short-term pollutant-limit convention. ISR entry addresses are 0x1000 for daily exceedance and 0x2000 otherwise; the sensor address is 0x3000. Which tuple gives (daily airborne concentration in normalized scientific notation, daily limit, selected interrupt-vector value), with concentrations in mol/m³?
explanation: The solution density is 1,180 g/L. Applying the NaOH mass fraction and molar mass gives a solution molarity of 0.16 × 1,180 / 40 = 4.72 mol/L. The collection volume is 1 cL = 0.01 L, so the collected amount is 4.72 × 0.01 = 0.0472 mol. Dividing by 1,000 m³ gives the daily-average airborne concentration, 4.72 × 10^-5 mol/m³. This is normalized scientific notation: the coefficient is at least 1 and below 10, and the exponent is an integer. Under the general convention invoked for these fictional limits, the longer-term daily limit is the lower value, 2 × 10^-5 mol/m³. The measured daily concentration exceeds it, selecting the daily-exceedance ISR. An interrupt vector identifies the ISR entry address, so its value must be 0x1000 rather than the sensor address 0x3000.

Knowing density, mass fraction, molar mass, and the centiliter conversion separately but failing to assemble the collected-amount calculation, instead treating 1,180 / 40 = 29.5 as collected moles without applying either the 0.16 mass fraction or the 0.01 L collection volume -> division by 1,000 produces 2.95 × 10^-2 mol/m³, which still exceeds the correctly assigned daily limit -> the option pairs that erroneous concentration with 2 × 10^-5 and 0x1000.

question:
Unconscious 78-year-old rescued from burning plastics/textiles: BP 70/35 mmHg, pulse 42/min; oxygen underway. Events: I external sensor-ready; II ordinary cache operation; III virtual-memory failure; IV floating-point underflow; V floating-point overflow. Overflow trapping enabled; underflow trapping disabled. Overflow invalidates environmental HCN=0.12 mol/m³; recovery validates 0.00012 mol/m³ (not diagnostic alone).
Trace checksum: S+a+n+H+T. S=sum of interrupt/exception event numbers; a×10ⁿ=published HCN (mol/m³), normalized.
H: 1=cyanide binds cytochrome-oxidase central ion, inhibiting cellular respiration; 2=hemoglobin binding blocks oxygen transport.
T: 1=prepare transcutaneous pacing immediately; 2=observe five minutes; 3=pace after recovery. Pacing unavailable: epinephrine/dopamine.
Which checksum represents the correct end-to-end trace?
explanation: The applicable sources are I, III, and V: the external sensor-ready signal, virtual-memory failure, and enabled floating-point overflow exception. Thus S=1+3+5=9. Ordinary cache operation and the stipulated nontrapping underflow do not qualify. Overflow invalidates the first computation, so publication must use the recovered environmental reading: 0.00012=1.2×10⁻⁴ mol/m³. This gives a=1.2 and n=−4, with 1≤|a|<10 and an integer exponent. Burning plastics and textiles can release cyanides; their binding to the central ion of cytochrome oxidase inhibits cellular respiration, so H=1. This is an exposure hazard, not a diagnosis established by environmental HCN alone. Unconsciousness, BP 70/35 mmHg, and pulse 42/min require an immediate response to unstable bradycardia: prepare transcutaneous pacing, using epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable. Care proceeds independently of software recovery, so T=1. The checksum is 9+1.2−4+1+1=8.2.

distractor_analysis.reason: Failing to recognize the supplied presentation as unstable bradycardia requiring immediate intervention → choosing five-minute observation, T=2, while retaining S=9, a=1.2, n=−4, and H=1 → checksum 9.2.

Knowing the interrupt sources, normalization rule, cyanide mechanism, and clinical response separately but failing to connect overflow invalidation to publication → normalizing and publishing the stale 0.12 mol/m³ result as 1.2×10⁻¹ instead of using the validated reading → checksum 9+1.2−1+1+1=11.2.

Treating CPU overflow as evidence of greater physiological poisoning severity and its recovery as a prerequisite for clinical intervention → delaying pacing until recovery, T=3, despite otherwise correct source classification, validated concentration, and cyanide mechanism → checksum 9+1.2−4+1+3=10.2.

question:
2. Discuss the formation process of marine erosion landform
answer:
geography.completion: A: The kinetic energy of the sea water movement, the dissolution of the sea water and the activities of marine organisms and other factors cause the destruction of the rocks on the coast and the seabed, which is called marine erosion. The mode of marine erosion includes mechanical denudation and chemical dissolution, but mainly mechanical denudation. There are two kinds of mechanical denudation: one is that the rock is destroyed by the rock alluvial by the sea water in the process of movement, which is called erosion; One is that the gravel sand carried by the moving sea water rubs and collides with the coast or the seabed, causing it to be damaged, which is called abrasion. The main driving force of sea erosion is sea waves. In the coastal zone composed of bedrock, the sea waves violently wash the coast with the surf and abrade the seabed and coastal rocks of the coastal zone with the gravel sand it carries. Tide can promote the destructive effect of waves in the open coastal zone. Under the continuous destruction of waves and tides, a groove extending along the coast is formed near the height of the waves at the base of the shore wall, which is called the sea erosion groove. The sea erosion groove continues to expand and deepen, and the upper rock of the sea erosion groove loses its support and collapses, forming a straight and steep rock wall, called the sea erosion cliff. If the sea erosion cliff retreats continuously under the action of sea waves, a slightly seaward inclined platform composed of bedrock is formed in front of the sea erosion cliff, which is called the sea erosion platform (or wave cutting platform). The bottom current carries the denuded coastal material 8 to the side of the sea water outside the wave cutting platform and deposits it to form the wave building platform. The bedrock column left on the wave cutting platform that has not been denuded is called marine erosion column. The sea erosion platform is continuously widened due to the sea erosion, so that the wave will pass more and more long distance when impacting the cliff foundation, and the energy consumption of the wave is increasing. Finally, all the energy of the sea wave is consumed on the sea erosion platform. The sea erosion tends to stop. After that, if the crust rises so that the wave cutting platform rises to the height that the sea water cannot submerge, the sea erosion terrace will be formed.

question:
2. Discuss the formation process of marine erosion landform
answer:
sample.completion: A: The kinetic energy of the sea water movement, the dissolution of the sea water and the activities of marine organisms and other factors cause the destruction of the rocks on the coast and the seabed, which is called marine erosion. The mode of marine erosion includes mechanical denudation and chemical dissolution, but mainly mechanical denudation. There are two kinds of mechanical denudation: one is that the rock is destroyed by the rock alluvial by the sea water in the process of movement, which is called erosion; One is that the gravel sand carried by the moving sea water rubs and collides with the coast or the seabed, causing it to be damaged, which is called abrasion. The main driving force of sea erosion is sea waves. In the coastal zone composed of bedrock, the sea waves violently wash the coast with the surf and abrade the seabed and coastal rocks of the coastal zone with the gravel sand it carries. Tide can promote the destructive effect of waves in the open coastal zone. Under the continuous destruction of waves and tides, a groove extending along the coast is formed near the height of the waves at the base of the shore wall, which is called the sea erosion groove. The sea erosion groove continues to expand and deepen, and the upper rock of the sea erosion groove loses its support and collapses, forming a straight and steep rock wall, called the sea erosion cliff. If the sea erosion cliff retreats continuously under the action of sea waves, a slightly seaward inclined platform composed of bedrock is formed in front of the sea erosion cliff, which is called the sea erosion platform (or wave cutting platform). The bottom current carries the denuded coastal material 8 to the side of the sea water outside the wave cutting platform and deposits it to form the wave building platform. The bedrock column left on the wave cutting platform that has not been denuded is called marine erosion column. The sea erosion platform is continuously widened due to the sea erosion, so that the wave will pass more and more long distance when impacting the cliff foundation, and the energy consumption of the wave is increasing. Finally, all the energy of the sea wave is consumed on the sea erosion platform. The sea erosion tends to stop. After that, if the crust rises so that the wave cutting platform rises to the height that the sea water cannot submerge, the sea erosion terrace will be formed.

Of 14,000 proposed records describing individuals' First Amendment activities, 10,000 have express authorization from the individuals concerned; the remaining 4,000 have neither individual nor statutory authorization and are unrelated to any authorized law-enforcement activity. Each record occupies 2 MB. Specify one common archive, no duplicate copies or overhead, and a hypothetical annual tariff of 16,000 yuan per pool plus 0.5 yuan per occupied MB. Ask which device from the source options is classified as shared, how much data may be maintained under the quoted rule, and the resulting annual budget.

answer_plans.plan: Identify C, disk, as the shared device in the source classification. Apply the quoted legal rule to include the 10,000 individually authorized records and exclude the other 4,000. Compute required capacity as 2 × 10,000 = 20,000 MB. Apply the fixed-plus-variable cost model once to the common pool: 16,000 + 0.5 × 20,000 = 26,000 yuan annually. Sharing does not reduce the bytes stored.
Identify disk as shared but ignore the restrictions on maintaining First Amendment activity records. Store all 14,000 records, calculate 28,000 MB, and budget 30,000 yuan annually.

Correctly explain that only 10,000 records qualify under the quoted rule and identify disk as shared. Separately calculate the proposed unfiltered archive's 28,000 MB and 30,000-yuan cost, then report that as the procurement budget without propagating the legal exclusion into sizing and costing.

Correctly exclude the 4,000 unauthorized records and initially compute 20,000 MB, but incorrectly divide capacity by the two departments because the disk is shared. Budget for 10,000 MB, producing the erroneous annual total of 21,000 yuan.

legal.necessity: Establishes why the agency cannot automatically maintain every proposed record.
Permits the individually authorized records and requires checking whether excluded records have statutory authorization.
Rules out the remaining exception for the 4,000 records stipulated to be unrelated to authorized law-enforcement activity.

financial.necessity: Includes the stipulated annual pool charge once rather than multiplying it by records or departments.
Applies the stipulated per-MB rate to the legally eligible archive's occupied storage.
Combines the fixed charge and volume-dependent charge into the final annual budget.

mathematics.necessity: Treats 2 MB per record as a constant proportional relationship.
Uses the legally permitted record count as the quantity in the size calculation.
Converts 10,000 eligible records into 20,000 MB, supplying the volume needed for budgeting.

question: Two departments of a hypothetical federal agency propose 14,000 First Amendment activity records. Apply only 5 U.S.C. §552a(e)(7). Individuals expressly authorize 10,000; the other 4,000 have neither individual nor statutory authorization and are unrelated to authorized law-enforcement activity. Each record occupies 2 MB. Both departments use one common archive, without duplicates or overhead. Its hypothetical annual tariff lists fixed cost: 16,000 yuan/pool; variable cost: 0.5 yuan/occupied MB. Under the traditional operating-system shared/dedicated device classification, which device choice, legally maintainable volume, and total annual budget accommodate all eligible records?

options.A: Tape drives and disks; 20,000 MB; 26,000 yuan/year.

explanation: The source classification identifies disk as a shared device, not the combined category of tape drives and disks. Section 552a(e)(7) permits the expressly individually authorized records. The other 4,000 records have neither statutory nor individual authorization and do not satisfy the authorized-law-enforcement exception, so they are excluded. The eligible archive occupies 10,000 × 2 = 20,000 MB. Sharing access does not reduce that volume. A total fixed-plus-variable budget includes the fixed pool cost once and the occupied-volume cost: 16,000 + 0.5 × 20,000 = 26,000 yuan annually.

distractor_analysis.reason: Ignoring the restriction on maintaining unauthorized First Amendment activity records includes all 14,000 proposed records -> storage becomes 28,000 MB and the annual budget becomes 16,000 + 0.5 × 28,000 = 30,000 yuan -> the option reports disk, 28,000 MB, and 30,000 yuan/year.

Determining legal eligibility and storage correctly but treating the volume-dependent expense as the complete budget leaves the fixed pool expense unintegrated -> the reported annual budget is only 0.5 × 20,000 = 10,000 yuan -> the option reports disk, 20,000 MB, and 10,000 yuan/year.

Inferring that any storage device serving the departments' common archive belongs to the shared-device class incorrectly transfers application-level sharing to operating-system device classification -> tape drives are included alongside disks even though the eligible volume and budget remain 20,000 MB and 26,000 yuan -> the option reports tape drives and disks, 20,000 MB, and 26,000 yuan/year.

original_plan.question_plan: Plan a question asking which storage procurement proposal provides the lowest total cost over a stated planning horizon while satisfying a supplied records-retention rule for several departments. Specify annual data volumes, an initially empty archive, no compression or replication, disk capacities, purchase and annual maintenance costs, and the traditional operating-system classification in which disks are shared devices. Require sizing a shared disk pool for all records that must remain available at the horizon.

answer_plans.plan: Apply the supplied legal retention period, sum departmental data volumes over the required retained years, and select the adequate shared disk configuration with the lowest purchase-plus-maintenance cost over the planning horizon.
Size shared disk storage for only the latest year's records, ignoring the mandatory multiyear retention requirement, and choose the cheapest configuration meeting that understated capacity.

State the correct retained-data volume, identify disks as shared devices, and calculate proposal costs, but choose the cheapest proposal overall without using the required capacity to exclude undersized proposals.

Calculate retention volume and ownership costs correctly but divide required capacity by the number of departments, incorrectly treating shared-device access as multiplying physical storage capacity; choose the cheapest proposal under that mistaken sizing rule.

legal.necessity: The supplied retention period determines why storing only the latest year's records may violate the rule.
Records still within their mandatory retention period must remain available, making adequate storage a compliance requirement.
The rule's applicability determines which departments' records must be included in the compliant archive.

financial.necessity: Each proposal's purchase cost contributes to its total cost and must reflect the complete disk configuration.
Maintenance charges must be accumulated over the stated planning horizon rather than counted for only one year.
The financial ranking must compare combined horizon costs among proposals that satisfy the required capacity.

mathematics.necessity: Departmental data volumes must be summed, not divided by the number of departments merely because storage is shared.
For an initially empty archive, retained volume uses only years generated by the horizon that remain within the retention window.
The lowest-cost choice must be selected only among configurations whose capacity is at least the required retained-data volume.

computer_science.reason: The traditional shared/dedicated device classification identifies disk as the appropriate shared device and excludes tape drives. Without it, C cannot be distinguished from A.

legal.reason: The statutory exceptions determine which records may be maintained. Without this rule, the eligible record count—and therefore storage volume and budget—remains undetermined.

financial.reason: Fixed-versus-variable cost treatment requires adding one pool's annual fixed charge to the occupancy-based charge. Without that treatment, the variable-only amount in B is not excluded by the volume calculation alone.

Each logical operand read requires a page-table access and a data access, giving 62,800 physical accesses. Apply fixed-plus-variable budgeting: 100 + 0.001*62,800 = 162.80 yuan.

Separately calculate 31,400 residents, state that a logical read requires two physical accesses, and state the fixed-plus-variable budget formula. Fail to connect population to workload, inserting only two accesses into the budget and reporting 100.002 yuan.

Scan one record per resident, with exactly one single-word logical operand read per record, wholly within one page. question:
Bank requirements: explicit domestic-storage guarantees covering every tier/replica; Pr(latency > 100 ns) ≤ .10.
Unassigned deterministic latencies: {10,1000,1,100} ns; standard memory hierarchy. Terminal tiers partition accesses.
Probabilities below: (auxiliary memory, cache, registers, main memory).

Proposal  Probabilities  Upfront/annual($k)
P  .05,.30,.50,.15  10/10
Q  .01,.25,.70,.04  110/0
R  .08,.40,.40,.12  0/60
S  .20,.25,.05,.50  20/20

Only location terms:
P: “Information may be transferred to, and maintained on, computers outside this country.” Third-party-sharing review: “Irrelevant.”
Q–S: “Every tier and replica shall remain within this country.”
Payments: two year-ends; 10% annual discount; no other costs.
Which proposal minimizes eligible present-value cost?
explanation: The standard memory hierarchy assigns 1 ns to registers, 10 ns to cache, 100 ns to main memory, and 1000 ns to auxiliary memory. Neither the latency set nor the probability columns presents that ordering. Since a miss means latency strictly greater than 100 ns, only accesses terminating in auxiliary memory miss. Applying total probability to the terminal-tier partition gives miss probabilities P = .05, Q = .01, R = .08, and S = .20. The location terms must be interpreted separately from the sharing-review label. P's permission to transfer information to and maintain it on computers outside the country does not supply an explicit domestic-storage guarantee. A finding that this clause is irrelevant to third-party sharing does not establish domestic residency: sharing recipients and storage locations are different questions. Q–S contain an affirmative domestic commitment covering every tier and replica. Thus only Q and R satisfy both requirements. With upfront cost U and annual payment C, present-value cost is U + C/1.10 + C/1.10². Costs in $k are P = 27.36, Q = 110.00, R = 104.13, and S = 54.71. R is therefore the least-cost eligible proposal. Discounting changes the comparison: R's undiscounted total is 120, above Q's 110.

distractor_analysis.reason: Treating the third-party-sharing review's 'Irrelevant' label as resolving domestic-storage compliance overlooks the clause's permission for foreign transfer and maintenance -> P is incorrectly admitted with miss probability .05 and the lowest present-value cost, $27.36k -> select P.

Computing the hierarchy mapping, risk, contractual eligibility, and discounted costs separately but choosing speed instead of minimizing eligible cost fails to combine those results under the stated objective -> Q is favored for its .01 miss probability and 17.2 ns expected latency over R's .08 and 96.4 ns despite costing $110k rather than $104.13k -> select Q.

Reversing the memory hierarchy assigns 1000 ns to registers, 100 ns to cache, 10 ns to main memory, and 1 ns to auxiliary memory -> the erroneous miss probabilities are the register probabilities, making S the only domestically guaranteed proposal apparently eligible at .05, although its actual miss probability is .20 -> select S.

geography.prompt:
question:
Multilayer detachment tectonics of continental lithosphere
answer:
geography.completion:
Working model Decollement/detachment layer refers to a relatively weak rock-structure combination layer above the underlying rock combination, controlled by the overlying folded rock combination, and characterized by strong shear deformation. Multiple detachment layers may develop simultaneously or continuously during lithosphere deformation, and detachment layers may develop on different structural scales, so multi-layer detachment tectonics is the main mode of lithosphere deformation. The discovery of large-scale low-angle faults, such as extensional detachment faults[1,2] and large-scale low-angle thrust faults[3,4], has led structural geologists to propose that the continental lithosphere may be stratified according to physical properties . Therefore, when the lithosphere undergoes large-scale structural deformation, structural detachment may occur along the physical property mutation interface, forming a lithosphere-scale decollement fault. These detachment faults divide the lithosphere into structural layers with different petrophysical properties. Due to the different depths and temperature-pressure conditions of each structural layer, the deformation behavior of each structural layer is also different. A variety of hypothetical models have been proposed for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere. For example, in the Himalayas, southern Tibet, and other orogenic belts, under the thickening of the lithosphere, it is proposed that the middle-crust channel (or channel) flow model (mid-crustal ductile channel flow) to adjust the excess mass, which explains the phenomenon of the coexistence of surface extension and compression structures[5~7]. Jackson [8]'s continental lithosphere sandwich structure model (Fig. 1) uses the relationship between lithospheric rock physical conditions and temperature and pressure conditions to explain the reasons for the occurrence and existence of delamination structures. Evidence problem
Fig. 1 	Jackson lithosphere sandwich structure model [8] The lithosphere multi-layer detachment structure model has been supported by some field observations and experimental evidence, mainly including: ① Field observation support. Since the deformation traces of the deep structural layers of the lithosphere can be exposed under tectonic action, in some special structural parts, the structural traces formed by different structural layers of the lithosphere during the same tectonic process can "co-exist". A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). The above shows that multi-layer detachment tectonics can develop in different structural layers of lithosphere. Fig. 2. 	Three delaminated tectonic models in the formation of low-angle normal faults and metamorphic core complex structures[1,2] Brittle upper crust; 2. Ductile crust; 3. Lithospheric upper mantle; 4. Asthenosphere; 5. Magmatic rock② Evidence from deep geophysical exploration. The most important evidence support for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere comes from the results of deep geophysical exploration, including deep seismic reflection, magnetotelluric sounding, and Bouguer gravity anomaly detection. After the 5.12 Longmenshan Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008, Burchfiel et al. [11], based on data such as the Bouguer gravity anomaly, believed that the upper crust of Longmenshan did not thicken significantly, but the middle and lower crust with one to several layers of ductile flow crust was flowing eastward. In the process, it was blocked and thickened by the hard central Sichuan block under the Sichuan Basin, resulting in the vertical uplift of Longmenshan and the accumulation of abnormal stress, which eventually led to the Wenchuan earthquake in May 2008. This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. [11] further proves that the passage (or channel) flow mode [5~7]. In many mountain ranges, detachment faults have been recognized as one of the dominant factors of orogeny, such as the use of deep reflection seismic profiling (CORCOP) to discover a huge near-horizontal fault beneath the Blue Ridge of the Appalachians in the United States Thrust detachment zone, and pushed the Precambrian crystalline rock series of the Blue Ridge on the sedimentary cover of the Lower Paleozoic, and the thrust distance from the southeast to the northwest of the 5-15km thick foreign rock sheet Up to 260km[3, 4]. ③ Supported by experimental simulation results. In order to verify the multi-layer detachment structure model of the lithosphere, people use petrological and geochemical analysis methods, or carry out relevant high-temperature, high-pressure and petrological experimental analysis on rock samples at different structural levels, and on this basis put forward The delamination structural model of the lithosphere [12] better explains the deep structural detachment of the lithosphere. Figure 3 	Formation model of multi-layered detached nappe thin-skinned structures in the South China Yangtze block [6] Fz, Fc, Fs and Ft represent the structural detachment of the Sinian base, Cambrian base, Silurian and Triassic lower parts, respectively Some key scientific issues involved in the detachment surface[10] Although the multi-layer detachment structural model of the continental lithosphere has been supported by some observations and experimental evidence, there are still some key scientific issues that have not been resolved. Therefore, the multi-layer detachment structural model It is still a working hypothesis. These scientific issues mainly include: ① How to determine the interface properties of structural layer detachment? That is, what is the underground originality? For example, the physical properties and deformation behavior of the structural layer interface are the most critical issues in the deformation of multi-layer detachment structures. What we have observed in the field is the structural traces of the lithosphere exposed to the surface after multi-layer detachment and deformation. However, the interface inferred from deep geophysical data has multiple solutions. How to compare it with surface observations becomes a solution. the crux of the matter. Some researchers have also proposed to use high temperature and high pressure experiments to test. However, due to the limitation of the strain rate and boundary conditions such as temperature and pressure during the experiment, the current simulation is far from the actual environment of natural deformation. ② What is the deformation process of structural layer detachment? That is, what kind of deformation and metamorphism process has it experienced? When we observe on the surface, we invert the deformation process according to some structural kinematics pointing signs during the deformation. However, during the observation process, it was also found that many kinematic directions at the same time were inconsistent or even opposite. In addition, the deformation process we are inverting now does not limit the time and deformation rate, and even completely ignores the deformation process. Therefore, this inversion process may be very different from the natural process. ③ Reasons for deformation differences between structural layers? Among the different structural layers observed in the field, there are huge differences in deformation structural styles and combinations, as well as the metamorphic temperature-pressure conditions reflected by them, but the interface between the two layers, that is, the ductile detachment shear zone, may sometimes only be a few centimeters. What is the reason, what is the tectonic process, and the tectonic force can cause such a huge deformation-metamorphism difference between the upper and lower structural layers? ④ How big is the scale of delamination? Since the multi-layer detachment is based on the observation of low-angle faults, the change and extension scale/depth of low-angle faults are the most important basis for determining the scale of delamination. However, there is no research example so far that can accurately determine The occurrence change and scale of low-angle faults to the deep. Another question related to this is whether this kind of delamination structure only occurs in the middle and upper part of the lithosphere, or can it occur in the entire continental lithosphere? For example, is the delamination at the bottom of the lithosphere[12] a type of delamination tectonics? ⑤ Is there really a middle and lower crustal ductile channel flow in the middle and lower crust? Is it one layer or several layers? Is the multilayer detachment tectonics of the lithosphere controlled by the flow of these ductile flow shells? Or to what extent can the ductile flow crust control the deformation of the lithosphere? How to determine the nature of this fluid? There are no definitive answers to questions about the relative viscosities or rheology of fluids. Since the above key problems have not been resolved, traditional structural geology field observations are limited by surface rock outcrops, there are uncertainties and multi-solutions in the interpretation of deep geophysical detection data, and rock geochemical data have limitations in geological relationship analysis. Insufficient, especially the boundary conditions set by experimental structural geology are far from satisfying the physical, chemical and geological reality of the deep deformation of the continental lithosphere. Therefore, only by combining the studies of structural geology, geophysics and rock geochemistry, and realizing the complementary advantages of multiple disciplines, can objectively carry out more in-depth research on the multi-layer delamination structure of the lithosphere. With the continuous refinement of field structural analysis and the discovery of new important evidence and key structural phenomena, coupled with the continuous application of modern testing and simulation techniques in the field of earth sciences, the temperature-pressure conditions at different depths of the lithosphere and their Morphing features will gradually become a reality. On the basis of these studies, the continental lithosphere multi-layer delamination model will be continuously revised and improved.
